bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =魏紀一=

translations.literal: = Wei Records 1 =
translations.idiomatic: Wei Records 1

sentences.zh: 起上章困敦，盡玄黓攝提格，凡三年。

translations.literal: Beginning with Shangzhang Kundun, ending with Xuanyi Shetige, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Wei Records 1] Spanning from the year Shangzhang Kundun through Xuanyi Shetige—a period of three years.

sentences.zh: 世祖文皇帝上

translations.literal: Founder Emperor Wen, Part One (upper)
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Wen the Founder, Part One

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，武王至洛陽；

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, King Wu arrived at Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, during the first month, King Wu (Cao Cao) arrived at Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 庚子，薨。

translations.literal: On the day Gengzi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengzi, he passed away.

sentences.zh: 王知人善察，難眩以偽。

translations.literal: The King knew men and was skilled at observation; difficult to dazzle with falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to read men and was keenly observant, so that falsehood could scarcely deceive him.

sentences.zh: 識拔奇才，不拘微賤，隨能任使，皆獲其用。

translations.literal: He recognized and promoted extraordinary talent, not confined by lowly status; according to ability he assigned duties, and all were put to use.
translations.idiomatic: He singled out men of rare ability without regard for humble birth, assigned each according to his talents, and put them all to work.

sentences.zh: 與敵對陳，意思安閒，如不欲戰然；

translations.literal: When facing the enemy in formation, his expression was easy and relaxed, as if he did not wish to fight;
translations.idiomatic: When arrayed against the enemy, he seemed calm and unhurried, almost as though he had no wish to fight;

sentences.zh: 及至決機乘勝，氣勢盈溢。

translations.literal: but when it came to decisive action and seizing victory, his momentum overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: yet once the moment for decision came and victory was within reach, his fighting spirit brimmed over.

sentences.zh: 勳勞宜賞，不吝千金；

translations.literal: Merit deserving reward, he did not begrudge thousands in gold;
translations.idiomatic: When merit merited reward, he did not spare a thousand pieces of gold;

sentences.zh: 無功望施，分豪不與。

translations.literal: those without achievement who hoped for favor received not a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: but those who sought favors without achievement received not a whit.

sentences.zh: 用法峻急，有犯必戮，或對之流涕，然終無所赦。

translations.literal: His use of law was stern and swift; if there was offense, execution was certain. Sometimes he wept before them, yet in the end there was no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law with severe urgency: offenders were sure to die, and though he sometimes wept in their presence, he never granted pardon in the end.

sentences.zh: 雅性節儉，不好華麗。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and did not love splendor.
translations.idiomatic: By disposition he was sparing and disliked lavish display.

sentences.zh: 故能芟刈群雄，幾平海內。

translations.literal: Therefore he was able to mow down the contending lords and nearly pacify all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was able to cut down rival warlords and nearly bring the empire under his rule.

sentences.zh: 是時太子在鄴，軍中騷動。

translations.literal: At this time the Heir Apparent was at Ye, and the army was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was then at Ye, and the army was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 群僚欲秘不發喪，諫議大夫賈逵以為事不可秘，乃發喪。

translations.literal: The officials wished to keep secret and not announce the mourning. Remonstrance Counselor Jia Kui held that the matter could not be kept secret, and so the mourning was announced.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers wished to conceal the death and not announce mourning, but Remonstrance Counselor Jia Kui argued that the affair could not be hidden, and mourning was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 或言宜諸城守，悉用譙、沛人。

translations.literal: Some said that city garrisons should all employ men from Qiao and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed that every city garrison should be staffed entirely with men from Qiao and Pei.

sentences.zh: 魏郡太守廣陵徐宣厲聲曰：「今者遠近一統，人懷效節，何必專任譙、沛以沮宿衛者之心！

translations.literal: Administrator of Wei Commandery Xu Xuan of Guangling said sternly: "Now near and far are united, and men are ready to serve faithfully—why must we exclusively employ those from Qiao and Pei to dampen the hearts of the long-serving guards!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan of Guangling, prefect of Wei Commandery, said sharply: "Now that the realm is united from near and far, and all are eager to serve, why should we rely solely on men from Qiao and Pei and thus discourage the hearts of the palace guards!

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 青州兵擅擊鼓相引去，眾人以為宜禁止之，不從者討之。

translations.literal: Qingzhou soldiers on their own beat drums and led one another away. The crowd thought they should be stopped, and those who did not obey should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou troops began beating drums on their own and marched off together. Many thought they should be stopped by force and that anyone who refused should be attacked.

sentences.zh: 賈逵曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Jia Kui said: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui said, "That must not be done.

sentences.zh: 」為作長檄，令所在給其稟食。

translations.literal: " He wrote a long dispatch ordering that wherever they passed, provisions be supplied to them.
translations.idiomatic: " He drafted a long proclamation ordering every locality along their route to furnish them rations.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵侯彰從長安來赴，問逵先王璽綬所在，逵正色曰：「國有儲副，先王璽綬非君侯所宜問也。

translations.literal: Marquis Zhang of Yanling came from Chang'an to attend and asked Kui where the late king's seal and cord were. Kui said with stern face: "The state has a designated heir; the late king's seal and cord are not what Your Lordship should inquire about.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhang of Yanling had come from Chang'an to attend the funeral and asked Kui where the late king's seal and ribbon were. Kui said sternly, "The state already has an heir designate; the seal and ribbon of the late king are not a matter Your Lordship should raise.

sentences.zh: 」凶問至鄴，太子號哭不已。

translations.literal: " When news of the death reached Ye, the Heir Apparent wailed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " When word of the death reached Ye, the Crown Prince wailed ceaselessly.

sentences.zh: 中庶子司馬孚諫曰：「君王晏駕，天下恃殿下為命。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Sima Fu remonstrated: "Our lord has passed away; the empire relies on Your Highness for its fate.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Sima Fu admonished him: "Our lord is gone, and the empire looks to Your Highness for its very life.

sentences.zh: 當上為宗廟，下為萬國，奈何效匹夫孝也！

translations.literal: You should above serve the ancestral temple and below rule ten thousand states—why act the private filial piety of a common man!
translations.idiomatic: You must tend the ancestral shrines above and govern the myriad realms below—why imitate the mourning of a private commoner!

sentences.zh: 」太子良久乃止，曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " After a long while the Heir Apparent stopped and said: "Your words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Only after a long while did the Crown Prince cease and say, "You speak rightly.

sentences.zh: 」時群臣初聞王薨，相聚哭，無復行列。

translations.literal: " At this time when the officials first heard the King had died, they gathered to weep and there was no longer any formation of ranks.
translations.idiomatic: " When the ministers had first heard that the King was dead, they had clustered together in tears with no regard for order.

sentences.zh: 孚厲聲於朝曰：「今君王違世，天下震動，當早拜嗣君，以鎮萬國，而但哭邪！

translations.literal: Fu said sternly in court: "Now our lord has left the world and the empire trembles—we should early pay homage to the successor to settle ten thousand states—yet only weep?
translations.idiomatic: Fu cried out sternly in court: "Our lord has departed and the realm is shaken. You ought to bow to the successor at once to steady the empire—yet all you do is weep!

sentences.zh: 」乃罷群臣，備禁衛，治喪事。

translations.literal: " Then he dismissed the officials, prepared the guard, and arranged mourning affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He then dismissed the assembly, posted the guards, and set the mourning in order.

sentences.zh: 孚，懿之弟也。

translations.literal: Fu was Sima Yi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was the younger brother of Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 群臣以為太子即位，當須詔命。

translations.literal: The officials thought that for the Heir Apparent to ascend, an imperial edict was required.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers held that the Crown Prince could not take the throne without an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 尚書陳矯曰：「王薨於外，天下惶懼。

translations.literal: Minister Chen Qiao said: "The King died abroad; the empire is fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Qiao said, "The King died away from the capital, and the realm is filled with fear.

sentences.zh: 太子宜割哀即位，以系遠近之望。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent should cut short mourning and ascend, to tie the hopes of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince ought to set grief aside and take the throne at once, to hold the hopes of men near and far together.

sentences.zh: 且又愛子在側，彼此生變，則社稷危也。

translations.literal: Moreover there is a favored son at hand—if each side bred change, the altars of state would be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with a favored son close at hand, any friction between them could put the altars of state in danger.

sentences.zh: 」即具官備禮，一日皆辦。

translations.literal: " Immediately the officials and rituals were all provided, completed in one day.
translations.idiomatic: " The requisite officials and ceremonies were prepared that same day.

sentences.zh: 明旦，以王后令，策太子即王位，大赦。

translations.literal: Next dawn, by the Queen's order, the Heir Apparent was enthroned as King with an edict of investiture, and a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, by order of the Queen, the Crown Prince was installed as King and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 漢帝尋遣御史大夫華歆奉策詔，授太子丞相印、綬，魏王璽、綬，領冀州牧。

translations.literal: Soon the Han Emperor sent Imperial Counselor Hua Xin bearing the edict of investiture, conferring on the Heir Apparent the seal and cord of Chancellor, the seal and cord of King of Wei, and appointment as Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Han emperor dispatched Imperial Counselor Hua Xin with the formal investiture, granting the Crown Prince the seals and ribbons of Chancellor and King of Wei and appointing him Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 於是尊王后曰王太后。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Queen was honored as Queen Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Queen was then honored as Queen Dowager.

sentences.zh: 2改元延康。

translations.literal: 2. The reign era was changed to Yancong.
translations.idiomatic: 2. The reign era was changed to Yancong.

sentences.zh: 3二月，丁未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 3. Second month, on the first day Dingwei, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: 3. In the second month, on the first day (Dingwei), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 4壬戌，以太中大夫賈詡為太尉，御史大夫華歆為相國，大理王朗為御史大夫。

translations.literal: 4. On the day Renxu, Grand Master of the Palace Jia Xu was made Grand Commandant, Imperial Counselor Hua Xin was made Chancellor of State, and Director of Justice Wang Lang was made Imperial Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: 4. On the day Renxu, Grand Master of the Palace Jia Xu was appointed Grand Commandant, Imperial Counselor Hua Xin was made Chancellor of State, and Director of Justice Wang Lang was made Imperial Counselor.

sentences.zh: 5丁卯，葬武王於高陵。

translations.literal: 5. On the day Dingmao, King Wu was buried at Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: 5. On the day Dingmao, King Wu was interred at Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 6王弟鄢陵侯彰等皆就國。

translations.literal: 6. The King's younger brothers, Marquis Zhang of Yanling and others, all went to their states.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The King's younger brothers, including Marquis Zhang of Yanling, all departed for their allotted domains.

sentences.zh: 臨菑臨國謁者灌均，希指奏：「臨菑侯植醉酒悖慢，劫脅使者。

translations.literal: Guan Jun, coordinator for Linzi fief, currying favor memorialized: "Marquis of Linzi Zhi, drunk and insolent, coerced and threatened the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Jun, the commissioner for Linzi, seeking favor, memorialized: "Marquis Zhi of Linzi, while drunk, acted with arrogant insolence and intimidated the imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 」王貶植為安鄉侯，誅右刺奸掾沛國丁儀及弟黃門侍郎廙並其男口，皆植之黨也。

translations.literal: " The King demoted Zhi to Marquis of Anxiang, executed Ding Yi of Pei, Investigator on the Right, and his younger brother Ding Yi the Yellow Gate Attendant and their male dependents—all were Zhi's faction.
translations.idiomatic: " The King degraded Zhi to Marquis of Anxiang, executed Ding Yi of Pei, Investigator on the Right, and his brother Ding Yi the Yellow Gate Attendant along with their male kin—all partisans of Zhi.

sentences.zh: ::魚豢論曰：諺言：「貧不學儉，卑不學恭。

translations.literal: ::Yu Huan's discussion says: A proverb says: "The poor do not learn thrift; the lowly do not learn respect.
translations.idiomatic: ::Yu Huan observes: A proverb runs, "The poor do not learn thrift; the humble do not learn deference.

sentences.zh: 」非人性分殊也，勢使然耳。

translations.literal: " It is not that human nature differs, but that circumstance makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: " This is not because human nature differs, but because circumstances compel it.

sentences.zh: 假令太祖防遏植等在於疇昔，此賢之心，何緣有窺望乎！

translations.literal: If the founding lord had restrained Zhi and the rest in former times, how could these worthy men's hearts have harbored covetous designs!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Founding Lord kept Zhi and the others in check from the beginning, why would these talented men's hearts have turned to ambition!

sentences.zh: 彰之挾恨，尚無所至；

translations.literal: Zhang's grudge had not yet reached fruition;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's resentment had not yet come to anything;

sentences.zh: 至於植者，豈能興難！

translations.literal: as for Zhi, how could he have raised turmoil!
translations.idiomatic: and as for Zhi, could he truly have stirred up trouble!

sentences.zh: 乃令楊修以倚注遇害，丁儀以希意族滅，哀夫！

translations.literal: Yet Yang Xiu was killed for his reliance and attention, Ding Yi and clan exterminated for currying favor—how pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yang Xiu died for his close attention to the heir, and the Ding clan was exterminated for seeking favor—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 7初置散騎常侍、侍郎各四人。

translations.literal: 7. For the first time, Attendant Cavalier and Attendant were each set at four posts.
translations.idiomatic: 7. For the first time, four Attendants-at-Large and four Attendants were appointed.

sentences.zh: 其宦人為官者不得過諸署令。

translations.literal: When eunuchs held office they could not exceed the rank of directors of various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs who held office might not rise above the heads of the various bureaus.

sentences.zh: 為金策，藏之石室。

translations.literal: A gold book was made and stored in the stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: A book of gold was cast and placed in the stone vault.

sentences.zh: 時當選侍中、常侍，王左右舊人諷主者，便欲就用，不調餘人。

translations.literal: At the time when Attendants and Cavalier Attendants were to be chosen, the King's old personal followers prompted those in charge to employ them at once without selecting others.
translations.idiomatic: When it came time to choose Attendants and Cavalier Attendants, the King's former intimates urged the appointing officials to install them immediately, without considering anyone else.

sentences.zh: 司馬孚曰：「今嗣王新立，當進用海內英賢，如何欲因際會，自相薦舉邪！

translations.literal: Sima Fu said: "Now the successor king is newly enthroned—men of talent throughout the empire should be advanced. How can you wish to seize the occasion and recommend one another!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fu said, "The new king has only just ascended. We ought to promote worthy men from across the realm—how can you seek to use the moment merely to recommend one another!

sentences.zh: 官失其任，得者亦不足貴也。

translations.literal: If offices lose their proper charge, even those who obtain them are not worth esteeming.
translations.idiomatic: When offices lose their proper function, even the men who gain them are not to be valued.

sentences.zh: 」遂他選。

translations.literal: " Others were then chosen.
translations.idiomatic: " Other candidates were chosen instead.

sentences.zh: 8尚書陳群，以天朝選用不盡人才，乃立九品官人之法；

translations.literal: 8. Minister Chen Qun, because the court's selection did not exhaust talent, established the law of nine ranks for appointing officials;
translations.idiomatic: 8. Minister Chen Qun, finding that imperial appointments did not draw on the empire's full talent, established the nine-rank system for selecting officials;

sentences.zh: 州郡皆置中正以定其選，擇州郡之賢有識鑒者為之，區別人物，第其高下。

translations.literal: every province and commandery set Rectifiers to fix selections, choosing worthy men of discernment in each province and commandery for the post, distinguishing persons and ranking them high and low.
translations.idiomatic: every province and commandery appointed Rectifiers to govern selection, choosing locally esteemed men of discernment for the role, sorting candidates and ranking them by grade.

sentences.zh: 9夏，五月，戊寅，漢帝追尊王祖太尉曰太王，夫人丁氏曰太王后。

translations.literal: 9. Summer, fifth month, day Wuyin, the Han Emperor posthumously honored the King's grandfather the Grand Commandant as Grand King and Lady Ding as Grand Queen.
translations.idiomatic: 9. In summer, the fifth month, on the day Wuyin, the Han emperor posthumously honored the King's grandfather, the Grand Commandant, as Grand King and Lady Ding as Grand Queen.

sentences.zh: 10王以安定太守鄒岐為涼州刺史，西平麴演結旁郡作亂以拒岐。

translations.literal: 10. The King appointed Zou Qi, Administrator of Anding, as Inspector of Liang Province. Qu Yan of Xiping rallied neighboring commanderies in rebellion to resist Qi.
translations.idiomatic: 10. The King appointed Zou Qi, prefect of Anding, as Inspector of Liang Province. Qu Yan of Xiping stirred neighboring commanderies to revolt and resist him.

sentences.zh: 張掖張進執太守杜通，酒泉黃華不受太守辛機，皆自稱太守以應演。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin of Zhangye seized Administrator Du Tong; Huang Hua of Jiuquan would not accept Administrator Xin Ji—each styled himself Administrator in response to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin of Zhangye seized the prefect Du Tong; Huang Hua of Jiuquan refused to obey the prefect Xin Ji—each proclaimed himself prefect in support of Qu Yan.

sentences.zh: 武威三種胡復叛。

translations.literal: The Three Tribes of Hu in Wuwei rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Tribes of the Hu in Wuwei rebelled once more.

sentences.zh: 武威太守毋丘興告急於金城太守、護羌校尉扶風蘇則，則將救之，郡人皆以為賊勢方盛，宜須大軍。

translations.literal: Wuwei Administrator Wuqiu Xing reported the emergency to Jincheng Administrator and Protector of the Qiang Su Ze of Fufeng. Ze was about to go to the rescue, but the people of the commandery all thought the rebels' strength was at its height and that a large army should be awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu Xing, prefect of Wuwei, appealed for help to Su Ze of Fufeng, prefect of Jincheng and Protector of the Qiang. Ze prepared to march to his aid, but the people of the commandery all said the rebels were at the height of their power and that they should wait for a major force.

sentences.zh: 時將軍郝昭、魏平先屯金城，受詔不得西度。

translations.literal: At the time Generals Hao Zhao and Wei Ping were first garrisoned at Jincheng and had received orders not to cross west.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Hao Zhao and Wei Ping were then stationed at Jincheng under orders not to cross westward.

sentences.zh: 則乃見郡中大吏及昭等謀曰：「今賊雖盛，然皆新合，或有脅從，未必同心。

translations.literal: Ze then met the great officers of the commandery and Zhao and the rest to plan, saying: "Now though the rebels are strong, they have all newly joined together; some may have been coerced and are not necessarily of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ze then met the chief officials of the commandery and Hao Zhao and the others to plan, saying, "Though the rebels are strong, they have only lately come together; some may have been forced to join and are not truly united.

sentences.zh: 因釁擊之，善惡必離，離而歸我，我增而彼損矣。

translations.literal: Seize on a quarrel and strike them—the good and bad will surely separate; separated and returning to us, we increase while they decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they are divided by quarrels—the loyal and the disaffected will part; those who leave them and come to us will swell our ranks while theirs shrink.

sentences.zh: 既獲益眾之實，且有倍氣之勢，率以進討，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Having gained the substance of increased numbers and also the momentum of doubled spirit, leading them forward to attack, breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Once we gain both more men and redoubled morale, we can lead them forward to attack and defeat them for certain.

sentences.zh: 若待大軍，曠日彌久，善人無歸，必合於惡，善惡就合，勢難卒離。

translations.literal: If we wait for a large army, days will stretch long; good men without a place to return will surely join the wicked; once good and wicked join, the momentum will be hard to separate at once.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait for a large army, time will drag on; good men with nowhere to turn will inevitably side with the wicked, and once the two sides fuse, it will be hard to break them apart quickly.

sentences.zh: 雖有詔命，違而合權，專之可也。

translations.literal: Though there is an imperial order, to violate it yet accord with expedience—one may take sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: Though we have orders to the contrary, to disobey them in the interest of expediency is permissible—we may act on our own authority.

sentences.zh: 」昭等從之，乃發兵救武威，降其三種胡，與毋丘興擊張進於張掖。

translations.literal: " Zhao and the rest followed him, then sent troops to rescue Wuwei, subdued the Three Tribes of Hu, and with Wuqiu Xing attacked Zhang Jin at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao Zhao and the others agreed, marched to relieve Wuwei, pacified the Three Tribes of the Hu, and with Wuqiu Xing attacked Zhang Jin at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 麴演聞之，將步騎三千迎則，辭來助軍，實欲為變，則誘而斬之，出以徇軍，其黨皆散走。

translations.literal: Qu Yan heard of it and led three thousand infantry and cavalry to meet Ze, saying he came to aid the army but in fact intending treachery. Ze lured and beheaded him, displayed the head to the army, and his faction all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu Yan heard of this, he led three thousand foot and horse to meet Su Ze, claiming he had come to help the army but in fact plotting treachery. Ze lured him in and executed him, displayed the body before the troops, and his followers all fled.

sentences.zh: 則遂與諸軍圍張掖，破之，斬進。

translations.literal: Ze then with the various armies besieged Zhangye, broke it, and beheaded Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ze then joined the other forces in besieging Zhangye, took the city, and executed Zhang Jin.

sentences.zh: 黃華懼，乞降，河西平。

translations.literal: Huang Hua was afraid and begged to surrender; the Hexi region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua, in fear, sued for surrender, and the Hexi region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，敦煌太守馬艾卒官，郡人推功曹張恭行長史事；

translations.literal: Earlier, Dunhuang Administrator Ma Ai died in office; the people of the commandery pushed Chief Clerk Zhang Gong to act as Chief Administrator;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ma Ai, prefect of Dunhuang, died in office, the people of the commandery chose Chief Clerk Zhang Gong to act as chief administrator;

sentences.zh: 恭遣其子就詣朝廷請太守。

translations.literal: Gong sent his son Jiu to go to the court to request an Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent his son Jiu to the court to request the appointment of a new prefect.

sentences.zh: 會黃華、張進叛，欲與敦煌並勢，執就，劫以白刃。

translations.literal: It happened that Huang Hua and Zhang Jin rebelled, wishing to join forces with Dunhuang; they seized Jiu and threatened him with bare blades.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Hua and Zhang Jin rebelled and sought to combine forces with Dunhuang, they seized Jiu and held a blade to his throat.

sentences.zh: 就終不回，私與恭疏曰：「大人率厲敦煌，忠義顯然，豈以就在困厄之中而替之哉！

translations.literal: Jiu in the end did not turn back and privately wrote Gong a letter: "The Elder leads and encourages Dunhuang; loyalty and righteousness are manifest—how could you abandon that because Jiu is in hardship!
translations.idiomatic: Jiu would not yield and secretly wrote to Gong: "Father, you have led Dunhuang with manifest loyalty and righteousness—surely you will not abandon that resolve merely because I am in peril!

sentences.zh: 令大軍垂至，但當促兵以掎之耳。

translations.literal: Let the great army be about to arrive—you need only hasten troops to take them from the flank.
translations.idiomatic: The main army is nearly here—you need only press your troops forward to take them from the rear.

sentences.zh: 願不以下流之愛，使就有恨於黃壤也。

translations.literal: I pray you will not, out of base affection, cause Jiu to harbor resentment in the yellow earth.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let a father's private love make me die with resentment in my heart.

sentences.zh: 」恭即引兵攻酒泉，別遣鐵騎二百及官屬，緣酒泉北塞，東迎太守尹奉。

translations.literal: " Gong immediately led troops to attack Jiuquan, separately sending two hundred iron cavalry and officials along Jiuquan's northern border to go east and welcome Administrator Yin Feng.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong at once led his troops against Jiuquan and separately dispatched two hundred armored horsemen with officials along the northern border of Jiuquan to go east and welcome the new prefect, Yin Feng.

sentences.zh: 黃華欲救張進，而西顧恭兵，恐擊其後，故不得往而降。

translations.literal: Huang Hua wished to rescue Zhang Jin but looked west at Gong's troops and feared attack from the rear, so he could not go and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua wished to rescue Zhang Jin but, seeing Gong's forces to the west and fearing an attack from behind, could not go to his aid and surrendered instead.

sentences.zh: 就卒平安，奉得之郡，詔賜恭爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Jiu in the end was safe and sound; Feng obtained the commandery; an edict bestowed on Gong the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu came through unharmed; Yin Feng took office in the commandery; and an edict enfeoffed Gong as Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 11六月，庚午，王引軍南巡。

translations.literal: 11. Sixth month, day Gengwu, the King led the army south on inspection.
translations.idiomatic: 11. In the sixth month, on the day Gengwu, the King led his army south on a tour of inspection.

sentences.zh: 12秋，七月，孫權遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: 12. Autumn, seventh month, Sun Quan sent envoys with tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: 12. In autumn, the seventh month, Sun Quan sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 13蜀將軍孟達屯上庸，與副軍中郎將劉封不協；

translations.literal: 13. Shu General Meng Da was garrisoned at Shangyong and was not in harmony with Vice-General of the Army Liu Feng;
translations.idiomatic: 13. Meng Da, a general of Shu, was stationed at Shangyong and was at odds with Vice-General of the Army Liu Feng;

sentences.zh: 封侵陵之，達率部曲四千餘家來降。

translations.literal: Feng bullied and encroached on him; Da led more than four thousand households of his command to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Feng bullied and oppressed him, so Da led more than four thousand households of his following to defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 達有容止才觀，王甚器愛之，引與同輦，以達為散騎常侍、建武將軍，封平陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Da had bearing, talent, and appearance; the King greatly valued and loved him, drew him to ride in the same carriage, made Da Attendant Cavalier and General Who Establishes Might, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pingyang Village.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da was a man of fine presence and ability, and the King held him in high regard, taking him into his own carriage. He appointed Da Attendant Cavalier and General Who Establishes Might and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 合房陵、上庸、西城三郡為新城，以達領新城太守，委以西南之任。

translations.literal: The three commanderies of Fangling, Shangyong, and Xicheng were combined into Xincheng; Da was made to lead as Administrator of Xincheng and entrusted with charge of the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanderies of Fangling, Shangyong, and Xicheng were merged into Xincheng, and Da was made prefect of Xincheng with responsibility for the southwest.

sentences.zh: 行軍長史劉曄曰：「達有苟得之心，而恃才好術，必不能感恩懷義。

translations.literal: Marching Army Chief Clerk Liu Ye said: "Da has a heart of grasping gain and relies on talent and loves stratagems—he surely cannot feel gratitude and cherish righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye, chief clerk of the marching army, said, "Meng Da is grasping by nature and prides himself on talent and stratagem—he will never repay kindness with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 新城與孫、劉接連，若有變態，為國生患。

translations.literal: Xincheng borders Sun and Liu in succession—if there is a change of situation, it will breed trouble for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng lies adjacent to the domains of Sun Quan and Liu Bei; if he turns disloyal, he will bring trouble upon the state.

sentences.zh: 」王不聽。

translations.literal: " The King did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The King would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 遣征南將軍夏侯尚、右將軍徐晃與達共襲劉封。

translations.literal: He sent General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang and General of the Right Xu Huang together with Da to strike Liu Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang and General of the Right Xu Huang, together with Meng Da, to attack Liu Feng.

sentences.zh: 上庸太守申耽叛封來降，封破，走還成都。

translations.literal: Shangyong Administrator Shen Dan rebelled against Feng and came to surrender; Feng was defeated and fled back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dan, prefect of Shangyong, turned against Feng and surrendered to Wei; Feng was defeated and fled back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 初，封本羅侯寇氏之子，漢中王初至荊州，以未有繼嗣，養之為子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Feng was originally the son of the Luo chieftain of the Kou clan. When the King of Hanzhong first came to Jing Province, having no heir yet, he adopted Feng as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Feng had been the son of a Luo chieftain of the Kou clan. When Liu Bei first came to Jing Province and had no heir of his own, he adopted Feng as his son.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮慮封剛猛，易世之後，終難制御，勸漢中王因此際除之；

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang feared Feng's fierceness and that after a change of reign he would in the end be hard to control, and urged the King of Hanzhong to remove him on this occasion;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang feared that Feng's fierce and unyielding nature would make him impossible to control after a change of ruler, and urged Liu Bei to eliminate him while the opportunity offered;

sentences.zh: 遂賜封死。

translations.literal: and so Feng was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: and Liu Bei ordered him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 14武都氐王楊僕率種人內附。

translations.literal: 14. Yang Pu, Di King of Wudu, led his tribesmen to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: 14. Yang Pu, king of the Di in Wudu, led his people to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 15甲午，王次於譙，大饗六軍及譙父老於邑東，設伎樂百戲，吏民上壽，日夕而罷。

translations.literal: 15. On the day Jiawu, the King halted at Qiao and gave a great feast to the Six Armies and the elders of Qiao east of the town, setting up performers and a hundred entertainments; officials and people offered longevity wishes, and at evening it ended.
translations.idiomatic: 15. On the day Jiawu, the King encamped at Qiao and held a great feast east of the city for the Six Armies and the elders of Qiao, with music, dancers, and a hundred sorts of entertainment; officials and commoners offered toasts for his long life, and the revels lasted until nightfall.

sentences.zh: ::孫盛曰：三年之喪，自天子達於庶人。

translations.literal: ::Sun Sheng says: The three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: ::Sun Sheng remarks: The three-year mourning obligation extended from the Son of Heaven down to the common people.

sentences.zh: 故雖三季之末，七雄之敝，猶未有廢衰斬於旬朔之間，釋麻杖於反哭之日者也。

translations.literal: Thus even at the end of the three later ages and the exhaustion of the seven powers, there had still been none who abolished the hemp mourning garments within a fortnight and a month, or laid aside the hemp staff on the day of the return wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even in the late Three Dynasties and the age of the Seven Warring States, no one had yet cast off the hemp mourning garments within a fortnight or set aside the mourning staff on the very day of the return wailing.

sentences.zh: 逮於漢文，變易古制，人道之紀，一旦而廢，固已道薄於當年，風頹於百代矣。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wen of Han, the ancient system was changed; the norms of human conduct were in one morning abolished—truly the Way had grown thin in that age and custom had declined for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Wen of Han the ancient rites were altered and the norms of human conduct cast aside overnight; the moral Way had already grown thin in his day, and custom had declined for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 魏王既追漢制，替其大禮，處莫重之哀而設饗宴之樂，居貽厥之始而墮王化之基，及至受禪，顯納二女，是以知王齡之不遐，卜世之期促也。

translations.literal: The King of Wei, having followed Han institutions, replaced their great rites; he was in the heaviest mourning yet set feasting and music, stood at the beginning of bequeathing to posterity yet ruined the foundation of kingly transformation; when he came to receive the abdication, he openly took two daughters—in this one knows his royal span would not be long and the allotted years of his house would be brief.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei, having followed Han precedent, set aside its great mourning rites: he was in the deepest mourning yet held feasts with music, stood at the threshold of handing down his legacy yet undermined the foundations of royal virtue; and when he accepted the abdication he openly took two of the former emperor's daughters as consorts—from this one may know that his reign would not be long and his dynasty's span would be brief.

sentences.zh: 16王以丞相祭酒賈逵為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: 16. The King made Chancellor Libationer Jia Kui Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: 16. The King appointed Jia Kui, Libationer to the Chancellor, as Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 是時天下初定，刺史多不能攝郡。

translations.literal: At this time the empire was newly settled, and inspectors for the most part could not control the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had only just been pacified, and most provincial inspectors could not keep their commanderies in order.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「州本以六條詔書察二千石以下，故其狀皆言嚴能鷹揚，有督察之才，不言安靜寬仁，有愷悌之德也。

translations.literal: Kui said: "The province was originally to inspect those at two thousand bushels and below by the Six Articles edict, so their reports all speak of stern ability and eagle-like vigor, having talent for supervision—not of quiet calm and generous kindness, having the virtue of harmonious ease.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "A province exists to inspect officials of two thousand bushels rank and below under the Six Regulations, so their reports praise stern efficiency and keen oversight—they do not praise quiet forbearance and the gentle virtue of easy government.

sentences.zh: 今長吏慢法，盜賊公行，州知而不糾，天下復何取正乎！

translations.literal: Now the chief officials treat the law lightly and bandits walk openly; the province knows yet does not correct—where shall the empire take its standard!
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief officials scorn the law and bandits walk abroad with impunity; if the province knows this and does nothing, what standard can the empire follow!

sentences.zh: 」其二千石以下，阿縱不如法者，皆舉奏免之。

translations.literal: " Of those at two thousand bushels and below who indulged and did not follow the law, he memorialized to have them all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized for the dismissal of every official at two thousand bushels rank and below who indulged wrongdoing and failed to enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 外修軍旅，內治民事，興陂田，通運渠，吏民稱之。

translations.literal: Externally he trained the army, internally he governed the people's affairs, raised dyke-fields, opened transport canals—the officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He trained the armies abroad and governed civil affairs at home, built irrigation works, and opened transport canals, winning praise from officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「逵真刺史矣。

translations.literal: The King said: "Kui is a true inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The King said, "Kui is a true provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 」佈告天下，當以豫州為法；

translations.literal: " He proclaimed to the empire that Yu Province should be taken as the model;
translations.idiomatic: " He proclaimed throughout the realm that Yu Province should serve as the model;

sentences.zh: 賜逵爵關內侯。

translations.literal: he bestowed on Kui the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: and enfeoffed Kui as Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 17左中郎將李伏、太史丞許芝表言：「魏當代漢，見於圖緯，其事眾甚。

translations.literal: 17. Left Commandant of the Center Li Fu and Grand Clerk Assistant Xu Zhi memorialized: "Wei should replace Han—this appears in charts and weft texts, and the instances are very many.
translations.idiomatic: 17. Li Fu, Left Commandant of the Center, and Xu Zhi, assistant director of the Astronomical Bureau, submitted a memorial: "Wei is destined to replace Han, as charts and prophetic texts show—and the evidence is abundant.

sentences.zh: 」群臣因上表勸王順天人之望，王不許。

translations.literal: " The officials thereupon submitted memorials urging the King to follow the hopes of Heaven and men; the King did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers then submitted memorials urging the King to heed the will of Heaven and the people, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙卯，漢帝告祠高廟，使行御史大夫張音持節奉璽綬詔冊，禪位于魏。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day Yimao, the Han Emperor announced sacrifice at the High Temple and sent Acting Imperial Counselor Zhang Yin bearing credentials with the seal, cord, edict, and investiture book to abdicate the throne to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yimao, the Han emperor announced the sacrifice at the High Temple and sent Acting Imperial Counselor Zhang Yin with credentials bearing the imperial seal, ribbon, edict, and investiture document to abdicate the throne to Wei.

sentences.zh: 王三上書辭讓，乃為壇於繁陽，辛未，升壇受璽綬，即皇帝位，燎祭天地、岳瀆，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: The King three times submitted writings declining; then an altar was made at Fanyang. On the day Xinwei he ascended the altar, received the seal and cord, took the imperial position, offered burnt sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the mountains and rivers, changed the reign era, and declared a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The King declined three times in writing, then an altar was built at Fanyang. On the day Xinwei he ascended it, received the seal and ribbon, and took the imperial throne; he offered burnt sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and to the mountains and rivers, changed the reign era, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸酉，奉漢帝為山陽公，行漢正朔，用天子禮樂；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day Guiyou, the Han Emperor was honored as Duke of Shanyang, using the Han calendar and employing the Son of Heaven's rites and music;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day Guiyou, the former Han emperor was honored as Duke of Shanyang, permitted to keep the Han calendar and the rites and music of an emperor;

sentences.zh: 封公四子為列侯。

translations.literal: the Duke's four sons were enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: and the duke's four sons were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 追尊太王曰太皇帝；

translations.literal: the Grand King was posthumously honored as Grand Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: the Grand King was posthumously honored as Grand Emperor;

sentences.zh: 武王曰武皇帝，廟號太祖；

translations.literal: King Wu as Martial Emperor, temple name Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu as Martial Emperor, with the temple name Taizu;

sentences.zh: 尊王太后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: the Queen Dowager was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: and the Queen Dowager was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以漢諸侯王為崇德侯，列侯為關中侯。

translations.literal: Han feudal kings were made Marquises Who Honor Virtue, and ranked marquises were made Marquises within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han princes were made Marquises Who Honor Virtue, and ranked marquises were made Marquises within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 群臣封爵、增位各有差。

translations.literal: The officials received enfeoffments and promotions each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers received titles and promotions in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 改相國為司徒，御史大夫為司空。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State was changed to Minister of Education, Imperial Counselor to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State was retitled Minister of Education, and Imperial Counselor was retitled Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 山陽公奉二女以嬪於魏。

translations.literal: The Duke of Shanyang presented two daughters as consorts to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Shanyang presented two daughters to become consorts of Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝欲改正朔，侍中辛毗曰：「魏氏遵舜、禹之統，應天順民；

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to change the calendar. Attendant Xin Pi said: "The house of Wei follows the succession of Shun and Yu, responding to Heaven and complying with the people;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to change the calendar. Attendant Xin Pi said, "Wei follows the succession of Shun and Yu, responding to Heaven and winning the people's assent;

sentences.zh: 至於湯、武，以戰伐定天下，乃改正朔。

translations.literal: as for Tang and Wu, they settled the empire by warfare and only then changed the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: only Tang and Wu, who settled the realm through warfare, changed the calendar.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『行夏之時，』《左氏傳》曰：『夏數為得天正，』何必期於相反！

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Use the calendar of Xia.' The Zuo Commentary says: 'Xia's reckoning obtained Heaven's standard'—why must we insist on the opposite!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Follow the calendar of Xia.' The Zuo Commentary says, 'Xia's reckoning obtained Heaven's true standard'—why insist on doing the opposite!

sentences.zh: 」帝善而從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor approved and followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 時群臣並頌魏德，多抑損前朝；

translations.literal: At the time the officials all praised Wei's virtue and mostly belittled the former dynasty;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the ministers all praised the virtue of Wei and mostly disparaged the former dynasty;

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍衛臻獨明禪授之義，稱揚漢美。

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalier Wei Zhen alone clarified the meaning of abdication and transfer, praising Han's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: only Attendant Cavalier Wei Zhen explained the meaning of the abdication and praised the virtues of Han.

sentences.zh: 帝數目臻曰：「天下之珍，當與山陽共之。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly looked at Zhen and said: "The treasures of the empire should be shared with Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor looked at Zhen again and again and said, "The treasures of the empire ought to be shared with Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 」帝欲追封太后父、母，尚書陳群奏曰：「陛下以聖德應運受命，創業革制，當永為後式。

translations.literal: " The Emperor wished to posthumously enfeoff the Empress Dowager's father and mother. Minister Chen Qun memorialized: "Your Majesty, with sagely virtue responding to the age and receiving the Mandate, founding the enterprise and reforming institutions, should forever be a model for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor wished to posthumously enfeoff the Empress Dowager's parents. Minister Chen Qun memorialized: "Your Majesty, having received the Mandate through sagely virtue and founded a new order with reformed institutions, ought to set a lasting precedent for posterity.

sentences.zh: 案典籍之文，無婦人分土命爵之制。

translations.literal: Examining the texts of the canonical records, there is no institution of women receiving land and bestowing ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The canonical texts contain no precedent for ennobling a woman's parents with lands and titles.

sentences.zh: 在禮典，婦因夫爵。

translations.literal: In the ritual canon, a wife follows her husband's rank.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual law, a wife takes rank from her husband.

sentences.zh: 秦違古法，漢氏因之，非先王之令典也。

translations.literal: Qin violated the ancient law and Han followed it—this is not the excellent canon of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Qin departed from ancient law and Han followed suit; this is not the true precedent of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此議是也，其勿施行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "This proposal is correct—do not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "This opinion is correct. Do not carry it out.

sentences.zh: 」仍著定制，藏之臺閣。

translations.literal: " He still set down the fixed regulation and stored it in the terrace archives.
translations.idiomatic: " He nevertheless recorded the regulation as fixed law and stored it in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 18十二月，初營洛陽宮。

translations.literal: 18. Twelfth month, for the first time the Luoyang palace was constructed.
translations.idiomatic: 18. In the twelfth month, construction of the Luoyang palace began.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝如洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day Wuwu, the Emperor went to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wuwu, the Emperor proceeded to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 19帝謂侍中蘇則曰：「前破酒泉、張掖，西域通使敦煌，獻徑寸大珠，可復求市益得不？

translations.literal: 19. The Emperor said to Attendant Su Ze: "Earlier when Jiuquan and Zhangye were taken, the Western Regions sent envoys through Dunhuang and presented large pearls an inch across—could we seek to buy more and obtain them?
translations.idiomatic: 19. The Emperor said to Attendant Su Ze, "When we pacified Jiuquan and Zhangye, envoys from the Western Regions came through Dunhuang and presented pearls an inch across—might we send to buy more of them?

sentences.zh: 」則對曰：「若陛下化洽中國，德流沙幕，即不求自至。

translations.literal: " Ze replied: "If Your Majesty's transforming influence pervades China and virtue spreads to the desert curtains, they will come without seeking.
translations.idiomatic: " Ze replied, "If Your Majesty's transforming influence fills China and your virtue reaches to the desert frontiers, such things will come without being sought.

sentences.zh: 求而得之，不足貴也。

translations.literal: To obtain them by seeking is not worth esteeming.
translations.idiomatic: What is obtained by seeking is not truly precious.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘿然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 20帝召東中郎將蔣濟為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: 20. The Emperor summoned Eastern Commandant of the Center Jiang Ji as Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: 20. The Emperor summoned Jiang Ji, Eastern Commandant of the Center, to serve as Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 時有詔賜征南將軍夏侯尚曰：「卿腹心重將，特當任使，作威作福，殺人活人。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict bestowed on General Who Conquers the South Xiahou Shang saying: "You are a trusted core general, specially fit for assignment—make might, make blessing, kill men, give men life.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict was issued to Xiahou Shang, General Who Conquers the South, saying, "You are a trusted commander of the first rank, specially charged with authority—to wield power, dispense favor, take life, and spare life.

sentences.zh: 」尚以示濟。

translations.literal: " Shang showed it to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " Shang showed it to Jiang Ji.

sentences.zh: 濟至，帝問以所聞見，對曰：「未有他善，但見亡國之語耳。

translations.literal: When Ji arrived, the Emperor asked what he had heard and seen. He replied: "There was no other merit—I only saw words of a perishing state.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji arrived, the Emperor asked what he had heard and seen. He replied, "I saw nothing commendable in it—only the language of a state about to perish.

sentences.zh: 」帝忿然作色而問其故，濟具以答，因曰：「夫『作威作福』，《書》之明誡。

translations.literal: " The Emperor flushed angrily and asked the reason. Ji stated it fully in reply and said: "As for 'make might, make blessing'—it is the clear admonition of the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor flushed with anger and asked why. Ji explained in full and added, "The phrase 'wield power and dispense favor' is an explicit warning in the Book of Documents.

sentences.zh: 天子無戲言，古人所慎，惟陛下察之！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has no jesting words—what the ancients were careful about. May Your Majesty examine this!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven does not speak in jest—this the ancients took seriously. I pray Your Majesty will consider it!

sentences.zh: 」帝即遣追取前詔。

translations.literal: " The Emperor immediately sent to recall the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor at once sent to recall the edict.

sentences.zh: 21帝欲徙冀州士卒家十萬戶實河南，時天旱，蝗，民饑，群司以為不可，而帝意甚盛。

translations.literal: 21. The Emperor wished to move a hundred thousand households of Ji Province soldiers' families to fill Henan. At the time there was drought, locusts, and the people were hungry; the various offices thought it could not be done, yet the Emperor's intent was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: 21. The Emperor wished to relocate a hundred thousand households of Ji Province soldiers' families to populate Henan. There was drought, locusts, and famine, and the various offices all said it could not be done, yet the Emperor's resolve was very firm.

sentences.zh: 侍中辛毗與朝臣俱求見，帝知其欲諫，作色以待之，皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: Attendant Xin Pi and the court officials all requested audience. The Emperor knew they wished to remonstrate and showed an angry face waiting for them—none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Xin Pi and the court officials all requested an audience. The Emperor knew they meant to remonstrate and waited for them with an angry expression—none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 毗曰：「陛下欲徙士家，其計安出？

translations.literal: Pi said: "Your Majesty wishes to move the soldier households—where did this plan come from?
translations.idiomatic: Pi said, "Your Majesty wishes to relocate the soldier households—what is the plan behind this?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿謂我徙之非邪？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Do you say my moving them is wrong?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Do you mean that my plan to move them is wrong?

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「誠以為非也。

translations.literal: " Pi said: "I truly think it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi said, "I truly believe it is wrong.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾不與卿議也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I will not discuss it with you.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "I will not discuss this with you.

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，置之左右，廁之謀議之官，安能不與臣議邪！

translations.literal: " Pi said: "Your Majesty, not considering me unworthy, placed me at your side and installed me among the planning and deliberation officers—how can you not discuss with me!
translations.idiomatic: " Pi said, "Your Majesty, not deeming me unworthy, placed me at your side and made me one of your advisers—how can you refuse to discuss this with me!

sentences.zh: 臣所言非私也，乃社稷之慮也，安得怒臣！

translations.literal: What your servant speaks is not private—it is consideration for the altars of state. How can you be angry at your servant!
translations.idiomatic: What I say is not for my private interest but for the altars of state. How can Your Majesty be angry with me!

sentences.zh: 」帝不答，起入內。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not answer, rose, and went within.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor made no reply, rose, and went inside.

sentences.zh: 毗隨而引其裾，帝遂奮衣不還，良久乃出，曰：「佐治，卿持我何太急邪！

translations.literal: Pi followed and pulled his robe. The Emperor shook his garment and would not return; after a long while he came out and said: "Zuozhi, why do you seize me so urgently!
translations.idiomatic: Pi followed and seized his robe. The Emperor shook free and would not turn back; after a long while he came out and said, "Zuozhi, why do you hold me so tightly!

sentences.zh: 」毗曰：「今徙，既失民心，又無以食也，故臣不敢不力爭。

translations.literal: " Pi said: "To move them now both loses the people's hearts and there is no food—therefore your servant dares not fail to strive with all force.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi said, "To move them now would lose the people's hearts and there is no food to sustain them—therefore I dared not fail to argue with all my strength.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃徙其半。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then moved half of them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then moved only half of them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗出射雉，顧群臣曰：「射雉樂哉！

translations.literal: The Emperor once went out to shoot pheasants and turned to the officials: "Shooting pheasants is delightful!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once went out pheasant hunting and said to his ministers, "Hunting pheasants is a great pleasure!

sentences.zh: 」毗對曰：「於陛下甚樂，於群下甚苦。

translations.literal: " Pi replied: "For Your Majesty it is very delightful; for the officials below it is very bitter.
translations.idiomatic: " Pi replied, "It is a great pleasure for Your Majesty, but a great hardship for your ministers.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，後遂為之稀出。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was silent; afterward he therefore went out for this rarely.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor fell silent, and thereafter went out hunting far less often.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，以議郎孔羨為宗聖侯，奉孔子祀。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, Proposal Gentleman Kong Xian was made Marquis Who Honors the Sage and attended to sacrifices to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, Proposal Gentleman Kong Xian was appointed Marquis Who Honors the Sage to preside over sacrifices to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 2三月，加遼東太守公孫恭車騎將軍。

translations.literal: 2. Third month, Liaodong Administrator Gongsun Gong was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: 2. In the third month, Gongsun Gong, prefect of Liaodong, was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 3初復五銖錢。

translations.literal: 3. For the first time the five-zhu coin was restored.
translations.idiomatic: 3. The five-zhu coin was restored for the first time.

sentences.zh: 4蜀中傳言漢帝已遇害，於是漢中王發喪制服，謚曰孝愍皇帝。

translations.literal: 4. In Shu it was rumored that the Han Emperor had already been harmed; thereupon the King of Hanzhong proclaimed mourning and put on mourning garments, giving the posthumous title Filial and Lamented Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In Shu word spread that the Han emperor had been killed; the King of Hanzhong thereupon proclaimed mourning, put on mourning dress, and gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaomin.

sentences.zh: 群下競言符瑞，勸漢中王稱尊號。

translations.literal: The subordinates competed in speaking of omens and portents, urging the King of Hanzhong to assume the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: His followers vied in citing omens and portents, urging the King of Hanzhong to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 前部司馬費詩上疏曰：「殿下以曹操父子逼主篡位，故乃羈旅萬里，糾合士眾，將以討賊。

translations.literal: Front Division Major Fei Shi submitted a memorial: "Your Highness, because Cao Cao and his son forced the ruler and usurped the throne, therefore journeyed ten thousand li abroad, gathered soldiers and masses, intending to punish the traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Front Division Major Fei Shi submitted a memorial: "Your Highness came ten thousand li from home and gathered an army because Cao Cao and his son forced the emperor and usurped the throne, intending to punish these rebels.

sentences.zh: 今大敵未克而先自立，恐人心疑惑。

translations.literal: Now the great enemy is not yet overcome yet you first establish yourself—I fear men's hearts will be doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: The great enemy is not yet defeated, yet you would first declare yourself emperor—I fear this will breed doubt in men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖與楚約，先破秦者王之。

translations.literal: Formerly the High Ancestor made a pact with Chu that whoever first broke Qin would be made king.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the High Ancestor agreed with Chu that whoever first defeated Qin would be made king.

sentences.zh: 及屠咸陽，獲子嬰，猶懷推讓。

translations.literal: When he had slaughtered at Xianyang and captured Ziying, he still harbored yielding and deferral.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he took Xianyang and captured Ziying, he still held back and deferred.

sentences.zh: 況今殿下未出門庭，便欲自立邪！

translations.literal: How much more now, when Your Highness has not yet gone beyond the gate and courtyard, yet you wish to establish yourself!
translations.idiomatic: How much less should you declare yourself emperor when you have not yet even marched beyond your own gates!

sentences.zh: 愚臣誠不為殿下取也。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant truly does not approve this for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish servant truly cannot approve such a course for Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 」王不悅，左遷詩為部永昌從事。

translations.literal: " The King was displeased and demoted Shi to Staff Member of Yongchang in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: " The King was displeased and demoted Shi to a staff post in Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙午，漢中王即皇帝位於武擔之南，大赦，改元章武。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day Bingwu, the King of Hanzhong took the imperial position south of Wudan, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era to Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day Bingwu, the King of Hanzhong took the imperial throne south of Wudan, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 以諸葛亮為丞相，許靖為司徒。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang was made Chancellor and Xu Jing Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was appointed Chancellor and Xu Jing Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：天生烝民，其勢不能自治，必相與戴君以治之。

translations.literal: ::Your subject Guang says: Heaven gave birth to the teeming people; by their nature they cannot govern themselves and must together raise up a lord to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: ::Your subject Guang observes: Heaven gave birth to the teeming multitude; by nature they cannot govern themselves and must together set up a ruler to govern them.

sentences.zh: 苟能禁暴除害以保全其生，賞善罰惡使不至於亂，斯可謂之君矣。

translations.literal: If one can prohibit violence and remove harm to preserve their lives, reward good and punish evil so that they do not reach disorder—this may be called a lord.
translations.idiomatic: If he can restrain violence, remove harm, and preserve their lives; reward the good and punish the wicked so that society does not fall into chaos—such a man may be called a lord.

sentences.zh: 是以三代之前，海內諸侯，何啻萬國，有民人、社稷者，通謂之君。

translations.literal: Therefore before the Three Dynasties, feudal lords within the seas were not merely ten thousand states—whoever had people and altars of state was commonly called a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Thus before the Three Dynasties, the lords within the seas numbered not merely ten thousand states; whoever possessed people and altars of state was commonly called a lord.

sentences.zh: 合萬國而君之，立法度，班號令，而天下莫敢違者，乃謂之王。

translations.literal: One who combined ten thousand states and ruled them, established laws and measures, issued orders and commands, and none in the empire dared disobey—this was called a king.
translations.idiomatic: He who united the myriad states under his rule, established laws and institutions, issued commands that none in the empire dared disobey—only such a man was called a king.

sentences.zh: 王德既衰，強大之國能帥諸侯以尊天子者，則謂之霸。

translations.literal: When kingly virtue had declined, a powerful state that could lead the feudal lords to honor the Son of Heaven was called a hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: When royal virtue declined, a powerful state that could lead the feudal lords in honoring the Son of Heaven was called a hegemon.

sentences.zh: 故自古天下無道，諸侯力爭，或曠世無王者，固亦多矣。

translations.literal: Therefore from antiquity when the empire was without the Way, feudal lords strove by force, and sometimes ages passed without a king—this too was common.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whenever the empire has lacked the Way, the feudal lords have fought for power, and ages have often passed without any true king—this too has been common enough.

sentences.zh: 秦焚書坑儒，漢興，學者始推五德生、勝，以秦為閏位，在木火之間，霸而不王，於是正閏之論興矣。

translations.literal: Qin burned books and buried scholars; Han arose and scholars first deduced the five virtues' birth and conquest, taking Qin as an intercalary position between wood and fire—hegemon but not king—and thus the debate over orthodox and intercalary arose.
translations.idiomatic: Qin burned the books and buried the scholars; when Han arose, scholars began to apply the theory of the Five Virtues in succession, treating Qin as an intercalary reign between wood and fire—a hegemony, not a true kingship—and thus the debate over legitimate and intercalary dynasties began.

sentences.zh: 及漢室顛覆，三國鼎跱。

translations.literal: When the house of Han was overturned, the Three Kingdoms stood like a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Han fell, the Three Kingdoms stood like a tripod.

sentences.zh: 晉氏失馭，五胡雲擾。

translations.literal: The house of Jin lost the reins; the Five Hu swarmed like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Jin lost control of the realm, and the Five Hu peoples swarmed over it like clouds.

translations.literal: The Zhu clan replaced Tang; the four quarters split apart; the Zhuye entered Bian—compared to the last rulers of Xia and Shang, their allotted years were all cast aside and not counted. These are all partial words of private interest, not the universal discussion of great impartiality.

These are all partisan words born of private interest, not the impartial judgment of great fairness.

sentences.zh: 臣愚誠不足以識前代之正閏，竊以為苟不能使九州合為一統，皆有天子之名，而無其實者也。

translations.literal: Your servant's foolish sincerity is insufficient to know the orthodox and intercalary of former ages; I venture to think that if one cannot make the Nine Provinces unite as one whole, all have the name of Son of Heaven but not the reality.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is truly too dull to judge which former dynasties were orthodox and which intercalary; I venture to think that unless the Nine Provinces are united as one, every claimant has the title of Son of Heaven but not the reality of rule.
