sentences.zh: 若以自上相授受者為正邪，則陳氏何所受？

translations.literal: If one takes those who receive succession from above as orthodox, then from whom did the house of Chen receive?
translations.idiomatic: If orthodoxy depends on receiving the throne from above, from whom did the Chen dynasty receive it?

sentences.zh: 拓跋氏何所受？

translations.literal: From whom did the Tuoba clan receive?
translations.idiomatic: From whom did the Tuoba clan receive the throne?

sentences.zh: 若以居中夏者為正邪，則劉、石、慕容、苻、姚、赫連所得之土，皆五帝、三王之舊都也。

translations.literal: If one takes those who occupy central China as orthodox, then the lands obtained by Liu, Shi, Murong, Fu, Yao, and Helian were all the old capitals of the Five Emperors and Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: If orthodoxy depends on holding central China, then the lands held by Liu, Shi, Murong, Fu, Yao, and Helian were all the old capitals of the Five Emperors and Three Kings.

sentences.zh: 若有以道德者為正邪，則蕞爾之國，必有令主，三代之季，豈無僻王！

translations.literal: If one takes those with virtue and the Way as orthodox, then tiny states must have worthy rulers, and at the end of the Three Ages, were there not perverse kings!
translations.idiomatic: If orthodoxy depends on virtue and the Way, then even the smallest states must have worthy rulers, and at the end of the Three Ages, were there not wicked kings as well!

sentences.zh: 是以正閏之論，自古及今，未有能通其義，確然使人不可移奪者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the debate over orthodox and intercalary, from antiquity to the present, has never had anyone who could fully grasp its meaning and make it so settled that no one could shift or wrest it away.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the debate over legitimate and intercalary dynasties, from antiquity to the present, has never produced a judgment so clear and settled that no one could challenge it.

sentences.zh: 臣今所述，止欲敘國家之興衰，著生民之休戚，使觀者自擇其善惡得失，以為勸戒，非若《春秋》立褒貶之法，拔亂世反諸正也。

translations.literal: What your servant now sets forth aims only to narrate the rise and fall of states and set forth the weal and woe of the people, so that readers may choose for themselves what is good or bad, gain or loss, and take it as admonition—not like the Spring and Autumn Annals, which established methods of praise and blame to pull a chaotic age back to the correct.
translations.idiomatic: What I now set forth aims only to narrate the rise and fall of states and record the weal and woe of the people, so that readers may judge for themselves what is good or bad, gain or loss, and take it as a warning—not like the Spring and Autumn Annals, which established a method of praise and blame to pull a chaotic age back to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 正閏之際，非所敢知，但據其功業之實而言之。

translations.literal: As for the boundary between orthodox and intercalary, that is not what I dare to know; I speak only according to the reality of their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: As for which dynasties were orthodox and which intercalary, I do not presume to judge; I speak only according to the reality of their achievements.

sentences.zh: 周、秦、漢、晉、隋、唐，皆嘗混壹九州，傳祚於後，子孫雖微弱播遷，猶承祖宗之業，有紹復之望，四方與之爭衡者，皆其故臣也，故全用天子之制以臨之。

translations.literal: Zhou, Qin, Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang all once unified the Nine Provinces and passed the throne to posterity; though their descendants grew weak and were driven abroad, they still inherited the work of their ancestors and retained hope of restoration, and those in the four quarters who contended with them were all their former ministers—therefore I fully employ the institutions of the Son of Heaven in treating them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, Qin, Han, Jin, Sui, and Tang all once unified the Nine Provinces and passed the throne to posterity; though their descendants grew weak and were driven into exile, they still inherited the work of their ancestors and retained hope of restoration, and those in the four quarters who contended with them were all their former ministers—therefore I fully employ the institutions of the Son of Heaven in treating them.

sentences.zh: 其餘地丑德齊，莫能相壹，名號不異，本非君臣者，皆以列國之制處之，彼此鈞敵，無所抑揚，庶幾不誣事實，近於至公。

translations.literal: As for the rest, their lands were alike in size and their virtue equal, none could unify the others, their titles were no different, and they were not originally lord and minister—I treat them all by the institutions of feudal states, each side matched as equals, with no elevation or demotion, so that the facts may not be falsified and the approach may come close to supreme fairness.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest, their territories were comparable in size and their virtue much the same; none could unify the others, their titles were no different, and they were not originally lord and minister—I treat them all by the institutions of feudal states, each side as an equal match, with no favor shown either way, so that the facts may not be falsified and the approach may come close to supreme fairness.

sentences.zh: 然天下離析之際，不可無歲、時、月、日以識事之先後。

translations.literal: Yet when the empire is split apart, one cannot do without years, seasons, months, and days to mark the sequence of events.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the empire is divided, one cannot do without years, seasons, months, and days to mark the sequence of events.

sentences.zh: 據漢傳於魏而晉受之，晉傳於宋以至於陳而隋取之，唐傳於梁以至於周而大宋承之，故不得不取魏、〔晉〕、宋、齊、梁、陳、後梁、後唐、後晉、後漢、後周年號<ref>故不得不取魏〔晉〕宋齊梁陳後梁後唐後晉後漢後周年號據胡注補。

translations.literal: According to Han passing to Wei and Jin receiving it, Jin passing to Song down to Chen and Sui taking it, Tang passing to Liang down to Zhou and Great Song succeeding it, therefore one must take the era names of Wei, [Jin], Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han, and Later Zhou<ref>therefore one must take the era names of Wei [Jin] Song Qi Liang Chen Later Liang Later Tang Later Jin Later Han and Later Zhou, supplemented according to Hu's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han passed to Wei and Jin received it, Jin passed to Song down to Chen and Sui took it, and Tang passed to Liang down to Zhou and Great Song succeeded it, I must therefore use the era names of Wei, [Jin], Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han, and Later Zhou<ref>[Editorial note: 'Jin' after 'Wei' supplemented according to Hu's commentary.]

sentences.zh: </ref>，以紀諸國之事，非尊此而卑彼，有正閏之辨也。

translations.literal: </ref>, to record the affairs of the various states—not honoring this one and demeaning that, making orthodox-intercalary distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] to record the affairs of the various states—not to honor one and demean another, nor to draw orthodox-intercalary distinctions.

sentences.zh: 昭烈之漢，雖-{云}-中山靖王之後，而族屬疏遠，不能紀其世數名位，亦猶宋高祖稱楚元王後，南唐烈祖稱吳王恪後，是非難辨，故不敢以光武及晉元帝為比，使得紹漢氏之遺統也。

translations.literal: The Han of Zhaolie, though said to be descended from Prince Jing of Zhongshan, was distant in clan affiliation and could not have its generations, ranks, and titles recorded; it is also like Song's High Ancestor calling himself a descendant of Prince Yuan of Chu, or Southern Tang's Founding Ancestor calling himself a descendant of Prince Ke of Wu—right and wrong are hard to distinguish—therefore I dare not compare them to Guangwu and Emperor Yuan of Jin, allowing them to continue the remnant succession of the house of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Han of Zhaolie, though said to be descended from Prince Jing of Zhongshan, was distant in clan affiliation and its generations, ranks, and titles cannot be reliably traced; it is much like Song's High Ancestor calling himself a descendant of Prince Yuan of Chu, or Southern Tang's Founding Ancestor calling himself a descendant of Prince Ke of Wu—right and wrong are hard to distinguish—therefore I dare not compare them to Guangwu and Emperor Yuan of Jin and allow them to continue the remnant succession of the house of Han.

sentences.zh: 5孫權自公安徙都鄂，更名鄂曰武昌。

translations.literal: 5. Sun Quan moved his capital from Gong'an to E and renamed E Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 5. Sun Quan moved his capital from Gong'an to E and renamed the city Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 6五月，辛巳，漢主立夫人吳氏為皇后。

translations.literal: 6. Fifth month, day Xinsi, the Han Ruler established Lady Wu as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: 6. In the fifth month, on the day Xinsi, the Han Ruler established Lady Wu as empress.

sentences.zh: -{后}-，偏將軍懿之妹，故劉璋兄瑁之妻也。

translations.literal: The Lady was the younger sister of General of the Left Yi and the former wife of Liu Zhang's elder brother Mao.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was the younger sister of General of the Left Yi and the former wife of Liu Zhang's elder brother Mao.

sentences.zh: 立子禪為皇太子。

translations.literal: He established his son Shan as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He established his son Shan as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 娶車騎將軍張飛女為太子妃。

translations.literal: He took the daughter of General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Fei as the Crown Prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: He took the daughter of General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Fei as the crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 7太祖之入鄴也，帝為五官中郎將，見袁熙妻中山甄氏美而悅之，太祖為之聘焉，生子叡。

translations.literal: 7. When the Grand Ancestor entered Ye, the Emperor was Commandant of the Five Offices of the Center; he saw Yuan Xi's wife, Lady Zhen of Zhongshan, was beautiful and was pleased with her; the Grand Ancestor arranged the betrothal for him, and she bore a son, Rui.
translations.idiomatic: 7. When the Grand Ancestor entered Ye, the Emperor was Commandant of the Five Offices of the Center; he saw Yuan Xi's wife, Lady Zhen of Zhongshan, was beautiful and was pleased with her; the Grand Ancestor arranged the betrothal for him, and she bore a son, Rui.

sentences.zh: 及即皇帝位，安平郭貴嬪有寵，甄夫人留鄴不得見。

translations.literal: When he took the imperial throne, Guo the Honored Consort of Anping had favor; Lady Zhen remained at Ye and could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the imperial throne, Guo the Honored Consort of Anping had his favor; Lady Zhen remained at Ye and could not see him.

sentences.zh: 失意，有怨言。

translations.literal: Disappointed, she had resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: Disappointed, she spoke resentfully.

sentences.zh: 郭貴嬪譖之，帝大怒。

translations.literal: Guo the Honored Consort slandered her, and the Emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo the Honored Consort slandered her, and the Emperor was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯，遣使賜夫人死。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day Dingmao, he sent an envoy to grant the Lady death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day Dingmao, he sent an envoy to order the Lady to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 8帝以宗廟在鄴，祀太祖於洛陽建始殿，如家人禮。

translations.literal: 8. Because the ancestral temple was at Ye, the Emperor sacrificed to the Grand Ancestor at the Jianshi Hall in Luoyang, using the rites of a family household.
translations.idiomatic: 8. Because the ancestral temple was at Ye, the Emperor sacrificed to the Grand Ancestor in the Jianshi Hall at Luoyang, using the rites of a family household.

sentences.zh: 9戊辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 9. On the last day of Wuchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 9. On the last day of the Wuchen cycle, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 有司奏免太尉，詔曰：「災異之作，以譴元首，而歸過股肱，豈禹、湯罪己之義乎！

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized to dismiss the Grand Commandant. An edict said: "When calamities and anomalies arise, they are to reprove the chief, yet blame is shifted to the arms and legs—is this the meaning of Yu and Tang blaming themselves!
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized to dismiss the Grand Commandant. An edict said: "When calamities and anomalies arise, they are meant to reprove the ruler, yet blame is shifted to his ministers—is this the meaning of Yu and Tang blaming themselves!

sentences.zh: 其令百官各虔厥職。

translations.literal: Let all the officials each reverently perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Let all officials reverently perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 後有天地之眚，勿復劾三公。

translations.literal: If hereafter there are calamities of Heaven and Earth, do not again impeach the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: If hereafter there are calamities of Heaven and Earth, do not again impeach the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 10漢主立其子永為魯王，理為梁王。

translations.literal: 10. The Han Ruler established his son Yong as King of Lu and Li as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: 10. The Han Ruler established his son Yong as King of Lu and Li as King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 11漢主恥關羽之没，將擊孫權。

translations.literal: 11. The Han Ruler was shamed by Guan Yu's death and was about to attack Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: 11. The Han Ruler was shamed by Guan Yu's death and prepared to attack Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 翊軍將軍趙雲曰：「國賊，曹操，非孫權也。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the Army Zhao Yun said: "The nation's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the Army Zhao Yun said: "The nation's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 若先滅魏，則權自服。

translations.literal: If we first destroy Wei, then Quan will submit of himself.
translations.idiomatic: If we first destroy Wei, Quan will submit of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 今操身雖斃，子丕篡盜，當因眾心，早圖關中，居河、渭上流以討凶逆，關東義士必裹糧策馬以迎王師。

translations.literal: Now though Cao's person is dead, his son Pi has usurped and stolen the throne; we should follow the people's hearts, plan early for Guanzhong, occupy the upper reaches of the Yellow and Wei Rivers to punish the wicked rebels, and the righteous men east of the Pass will surely pack provisions and spur their horses to welcome the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Now though Cao Cao is dead, his son Pi has usurped the throne; we should follow the people's hearts, move early to seize Guanzhong, hold the upper reaches of the Yellow and Wei Rivers to punish the wicked rebels, and the righteous men east of the Pass will surely pack provisions and spur their horses to welcome the royal army.

sentences.zh: 不應置魏，先與吳戰。

translations.literal: We should not set Wei aside and first fight Wu.
translations.idiomatic: We should not set Wei aside and fight Wu first.

sentences.zh: 兵勢一交，不得卒解，非策之上也。

translations.literal: Once the armies clash, they cannot quickly be disengaged—this is not the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armies clash, they cannot quickly be disengaged—this is not the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 」群臣諫者甚眾，漢主皆不聽。

translations.literal: " Many among the officials remonstrated, but the Han Ruler would not listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: " Many officials remonstrated, but the Han Ruler would not listen to any of them.

sentences.zh: 廣漢處士秦宓陳天時必無利，坐下獄幽閉，然後貸出。

translations.literal: The reclusive scholar of Guanghan, Qin Mi, stated that the season and time would certainly bring no advantage; he was made to sit down, imprisoned and confined, and then released on bail.
translations.idiomatic: The reclusive scholar of Guanghan, Qin Mi, argued that the season and time would certainly bring no advantage; he was thrown into prison and confined, and then released on bail.

sentences.zh: 初，車騎將軍張飛，雄壯威猛亞於關羽；

translations.literal: Earlier, General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Fei was heroic, strong, and fierce, second only to Guan Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Fei was heroic, strong, and fierce, second only to Guan Yu;

sentences.zh: 羽善待卒伍而驕於士大夫，飛愛禮君子而不恤軍人。

translations.literal: Yu treated the rank and file well but was arrogant toward the scholar-officials; Fei loved and honored gentlemen but did not care for the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu treated the rank and file well but was arrogant toward scholar-officials; Fei loved and honored gentlemen but did not care for the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 漢主常戒飛曰：「卿刑殺既過差，又日鞭撾健兒而令在左右，此取禍之道也。

translations.literal: The Han Ruler often warned Fei: "Your punishments and executions are already excessive, and you daily whip and beat strong youths yet keep them at your side—this is the way to invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Ruler often warned Fei: "Your punishments and executions are already excessive, and you daily whip and beat strong youths yet keep them at your side—this is the way to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 」飛猶不悛。

translations.literal: " Fei still did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei still did not reform.

sentences.zh: 漢主將伐孫權，飛當率兵萬人自閬中會江州。

translations.literal: The Han Ruler was about to attack Sun Quan; Fei was to lead ten thousand troops from Langzhong to join at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Ruler was about to attack Sun Quan; Fei was to lead ten thousand troops from Langzhong to join him at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨發，其帳下將張達、范彊殺飛，以其首順流奔孫權。

translations.literal: Just before setting out, his subordinate generals Zhang Da and Fan Qiang killed Fei, took his head, and fled downstream to Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Just before setting out, his subordinate generals Zhang Da and Fan Qiang killed Fei, took his head, and fled downstream to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 漢主聞飛營都督有表，曰：「噫，飛死矣！

translations.literal: The Han Ruler heard that the camp commander of Fei's camp had submitted a memorial and said: "Alas, Fei is dead!
translations.idiomatic: The Han Ruler heard that the camp commander of Fei's camp had submitted a memorial and said: "Alas, Fei is dead!

sentences.zh: ::陳壽評曰：關羽、張飛皆稱萬人之敵，為世虎臣。

translations.literal: ::Chen Shou's appraisal says: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were both called foes of ten thousand men, tiger ministers of their age.
translations.idiomatic: ::Chen Shou's appraisal says: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were both called match for ten thousand men, tiger ministers of their age.

sentences.zh: 羽報效曹公，飛義釋嚴顏，並有國士之風。

translations.literal: Yu repaid Lord Cao in service; Fei in righteousness released Yan Yan—both had the bearing of men of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yu repaid Lord Cao in service; Fei in righteousness released Yan Yan—both had the bearing of true men of the realm.

sentences.zh: 然羽剛而自矜，飛暴而無恩，以短取敗，理數之常也。

translations.literal: Yet Yu was stubborn and self-conceited; Fei was violent and without kindness—they failed through their faults, the constant pattern of principle and fate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu was stubborn and self-conceited; Fei was violent and without kindness—they failed through their faults, the constant pattern of fate.

sentences.zh: 12秋，七月，漢主自率諸軍擊孫權，權遣使求和於漢。

translations.literal: 12. Autumn, seventh month, the Han Ruler personally led the armies to attack Sun Quan; Quan sent envoys to sue for peace with Han.
translations.idiomatic: 12. In the seventh month of autumn, the Han Ruler personally led the armies to attack Sun Quan; Quan sent envoys to sue for peace with Han.

sentences.zh: 南郡太守諸葛瑾遺漢主箋曰：「陛下以關羽之親，何如先帝？

translations.literal: The Administrator of Nan Commandery, Zhuge Jin, sent a letter to the Han Ruler saying: "Your Majesty, compared with the Late Emperor, how close were you to Guan Yu?
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Nan Commandery, Zhuge Jin, sent a letter to the Han Ruler saying: "Your Majesty, compared with the Late Emperor, how close were you to Guan Yu?

sentences.zh: 荊州大小，孰與海內？

translations.literal: The size of Jing Province—how does it compare with all within the seas?
translations.idiomatic: How does the size of Jing Province compare with the whole empire?

sentences.zh: 俱應仇疾，誰當先後？

translations.literal: Both should be hated as enemies—who should come first and who after?
translations.idiomatic: Both should be hated as enemies—which should come first and which after?

sentences.zh: 若審此數，易於反掌矣。

translations.literal: If you examine these reckonings, it is easier than turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: If you weigh these points, the answer is easier than turning over your hand.

sentences.zh: 」漢主不聽。

translations.literal: " The Han Ruler would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han Ruler would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時或言瑾別遣親人與漢主相聞者，權曰：「孤與子瑜，有死生不易之誓，子瑜之不負孤，猶孤之不負子瑜也。

translations.literal: At the time some said Jin had separately sent close kin to communicate with the Han Ruler. Quan said: "I and Ziyu have an oath unchanging in life or death; Ziyu's not failing me is like my not failing Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some said Jin had separately sent close kin to communicate with the Han Ruler. Quan said: "Ziyu and I have an oath unchanging in life or death; Ziyu's loyalty to me is like my loyalty to Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 」然謗言流聞於外，陸遜表明瑾必無此，宜有以散其意。

translations.literal: " Yet slander spread abroad; Lu Xun made clear that Jin certainly had not done this and that something should be done to dispel such suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet slander spread abroad; Lu Xun made clear that Jin certainly had not done this and that something should be done to dispel such suspicions.

sentences.zh: 權報曰：「子瑜與孤從事積年，恩如骨肉，深相明究。

translations.literal: Quan replied: "Ziyu has served with me for many years; our kindness is like flesh and bone, and we understand each other deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Quan replied: "Ziyu has served with me for many years; our bond is like flesh and bone, and we understand each other deeply.

sentences.zh: 其為人，非道不行，非義不言。

translations.literal: As a man, what is not the Way he will not do; what is not righteous he will not say.
translations.idiomatic: As a man, he will not act against the Way or speak against righteousness.

sentences.zh: 玄德昔遣孔明至吳，孤嘗語子瑜曰：『卿與孔明同產，且弟隨兄，於義為順，何以不留孔明？

translations.literal: When Xuande once sent Kongming to Wu, I once said to Ziyu: 'You and Kongming were born of the same mother, and the younger follows the elder—in righteousness that is fitting—why not keep Kongming?
translations.idiomatic: When Xuande once sent Kongming to Wu, I once said to Ziyu: 'You and Kongming were born of the same mother, and the younger follows the elder—in righteousness that is fitting—why not keep Kongming?

sentences.zh: 孔明若留從卿者，孤當以書解玄德，意自隨人耳。

translations.literal: If Kongming stayed and followed you, I would write to Xuande to explain—his heart would follow the man.
translations.idiomatic: If Kongming stayed and followed you, I would write to Xuande to explain—his heart would follow the man he chose.

sentences.zh: 』子瑜答孤言：『弟亮已失身於人。

translations.literal: ' Ziyu answered me: 'My younger brother Liang has already given himself to another.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ziyu answered me: 'My younger brother Liang has already pledged himself to another.

sentences.zh: 委質定分，義無二心。

translations.literal: Having entrusted his person and fixed his station, in righteousness he has no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: Having pledged his loyalty and fixed his station, in righteousness he has no second heart.

sentences.zh: 弟之不留，猶瑾之不往也。

translations.literal: My brother's not staying is like Jin's not going.
translations.idiomatic: My brother's not staying is like my not going.

sentences.zh: 』其言足貫神明，今豈當有此乎！

translations.literal: ' His words could pierce through to the spirits—how could he now do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: ' His words could pierce through to the spirits—how could he now do such a thing!

sentences.zh: 前得妄語文疏，即封示子瑜，並手筆與之。

translations.literal: When I earlier received the slanderous letter, I immediately sealed it and showed it to Ziyu, and gave it to him in my own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When I earlier received the slanderous letter, I immediately sealed it and showed it to Ziyu, and gave it to him in my own hand.

sentences.zh: 孤與子瑜可謂神交，非外言所間，知卿意至，輒封來表以示子瑜，使知卿意。

translations.literal: I and Ziyu may be called joined in spirit; outside words cannot divide us. Knowing your intent has reached me, I immediately seal the memorial you sent and show it to Ziyu, so that he may know your intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu and I may be called joined in spirit; outside words cannot divide us. Knowing your intent has reached me, I immediately seal the memorial you sent and show it to Ziyu, so that he may know your intent.

sentences.zh: 漢主遣將軍吳班、馮習攻破權將李異、劉阿等於巫，進軍秭歸，兵四萬餘人，武陵蠻夷皆遣使往請兵。

translations.literal: The Han Ruler sent Generals Wu Ban and Feng Xi to defeat Quan's generals Li Yi, Liu E, and others at Wu, advanced the army to Zigui with more than forty thousand troops, and the barbarians of Wuling all sent envoys to request troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Ruler sent Generals Wu Ban and Feng Xi to defeat Quan's generals Li Yi, Liu E, and others at Wu, advanced the army to Zigui with more than forty thousand troops, and the tribal peoples of Wuling all sent envoys to request troops.

sentences.zh: 權以鎮西將軍陸遜為大都督、假節，督將軍朱然、潘璋、宋謙、韓當、徐盛、鮮于丹、孫桓等五萬人拒之。

translations.literal: Quan made General Who Pacifies the West Lu Xun Grand Commander with provisional credentials and put him in command of Generals Zhu Ran, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, Han Dang, Xu Sheng, Xianyu Dan, Sun Huan, and others—fifty thousand men—to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan made General Who Pacifies the West Lu Xun grand commander with provisional credentials and put him in command of Generals Zhu Ran, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, Han Dang, Xu Sheng, Xianyu Dan, Sun Huan, and others—fifty thousand men—to resist them.

sentences.zh: 13皇弟鄢陵侯彰、宛侯據、魯陽侯宇、譙侯林、贊侯兗、襄邑侯峻、弘農侯幹、壽春侯彪、歷城侯徽、平輿侯茂皆進爵為公；

translations.literal: 13. The Emperor's younger brothers, the Marquis of Yanling Zhang, the Marquis of Wan Ju, the Marquis of Luyang Yu, the Marquis of Qiao Lin, the Marquis of Zan Yan, the Marquis of Xiangyi Jun, the Marquis of Hongnong Gan, the Marquis of Shouchun Biao, the Marquis of Licheng Hui, and the Marquis of Pingyu Mao were all promoted in rank to duke;
translations.idiomatic: 13. The Emperor's younger brothers, the Marquis of Yanling Zhang, the Marquis of Wan Ju, the Marquis of Luyang Yu, the Marquis of Qiao Lin, the Marquis of Zan Yan, the Marquis of Xiangyi Jun, the Marquis of Hongnong Gan, the Marquis of Shouchun Biao, the Marquis of Licheng Hui, and the Marquis of Pingyu Mao were all promoted in rank to duke;

sentences.zh: 安鄉侯植改封鄄城侯。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Anxiang Zhi was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Anxiang Zhi was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 14築陵雲臺。

translations.literal: 14. The Lingyun Terrace was built.
translations.idiomatic: 14. The Lingyun Terrace was built.

sentences.zh: 15初，帝詔群臣令料劉備當為關羽出報孫權否，眾議-{咸云}-：「蜀小國耳，名將唯羽。

translations.literal: 15. Earlier, the Emperor ordered the officials to estimate whether Liu Bei would march out to avenge Guan Yu against Sun Quan; the assembly all said: "Shu is a small state; its famous general was only Yu.
translations.idiomatic: 15. Earlier, the Emperor ordered the officials to estimate whether Liu Bei would march out to avenge Guan Yu against Sun Quan; the assembly all said: "Shu is a small state; its famous general was only Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽死軍破，國內憂懼，無緣復出。

translations.literal: Yu died and the army was broken; within the state there is worry and fear—there is no occasion to march out again.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is dead and the army is broken; within the state there is worry and fear—there is no occasion to march out again.

sentences.zh: 」侍中劉曄獨曰：「蜀雖狹弱，而備之謀欲以威武自強，勢必用眾以示有餘。

translations.literal: " Attendant Liu Ye alone said: "Though Shu is narrow and weak, Bei's plan is to strengthen himself by might and majesty; the situation will surely require using many troops to show he has surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant Liu Ye alone said: "Though Shu is narrow and weak, Bei's plan is to strengthen himself by might and majesty; the situation will surely require using many troops to show he has surplus strength.

sentences.zh: 且關羽與備，義為君臣，恩猶父子。

translations.literal: Moreover, Guan Yu and Bei were righteous as lord and minister, and their kindness was like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Guan Yu and Bei were righteous as lord and minister, and their bond was like father and son.

sentences.zh: 羽死，不能為興軍報敵，於終始之分不足矣。

translations.literal: Yu died, and if he cannot raise an army to avenge the enemy, he falls short of the duty from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is dead, and if he cannot raise an army to avenge the enemy, he falls short of the duty owed from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 八月，孫權遣使稱臣，卑辭奉章，並送于禁等還。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Sun Quan sent envoys declaring himself a subject, with humble words presenting a memorial, and also returned Yu Jin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Sun Quan sent envoys declaring himself a subject, with humble words presenting a memorial, and also returned Yu Jin and the others.

sentences.zh: 朝臣皆賀，劉曄獨曰：「權無故求降，必內有急。

translations.literal: The court officials all congratulated him; Liu Ye alone said: "Quan seeks to surrender without cause—there must be urgency within.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials all congratulated him; Liu Ye alone said: "Quan seeks to surrender without cause—there must be urgency within.

sentences.zh: 權前襲殺關羽，劉備必大興師伐之。

translations.literal: Quan earlier launched a surprise attack and killed Guan Yu; Liu Bei will surely raise a great army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan earlier launched a surprise attack and killed Guan Yu; Liu Bei will surely raise a great army to attack him.

sentences.zh: 外有強寇，眾心不安，又恐中國往乘其釁，故委地求降，一以卻中國之兵，二假中國之援，以強其眾而疑敵人耳。

translations.literal: Externally there is a strong foe; the people's hearts are unsettled; he also fears the Central State will go and seize his opening—therefore he yields territory and seeks surrender: first to repel the Central State's army, second to borrow the Central State's aid, to strengthen his masses and make the enemy doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Externally there is a strong foe; the people's hearts are unsettled; he also fears the Central State will seize the opportunity to strike—therefore he yields territory and seeks surrender: first to repel the Central State's army, second to borrow the Central State's aid, to strengthen his forces and make the enemy hesitate.

sentences.zh: 天下三分，中國十有其八。

translations.literal: The empire is divided in three; the Central State has eight parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is divided in three; the Central State holds eight parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀各保一州，阻山依水，有急相救，此小國之利也。

translations.literal: Wu and Shu each hold one province, blocked by mountains and relying on rivers; when urgent they rescue each other—this is the advantage of small states.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu each hold one province, blocked by mountains and relying on rivers; when urgent they rescue each other—this is the advantage of small states.

sentences.zh: 今還自相攻，天亡之也，宜大興師，逕渡江襲之。

translations.literal: Now they turn and attack each other—Heaven is destroying them; we should raise a great army and cross the river directly to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Now they turn and attack each other—Heaven is destroying them; we should raise a great army and cross the river directly to strike them.

sentences.zh: 蜀攻其外，我襲其內，吳之亡不出旬〔月〕(

sentences.zh: 吳亡則蜀孤，若割吳之半以與蜀，蜀固不能久存，況蜀得其外，我得其內乎！

translations.literal: If Wu falls, then Shu is isolated; if half of Wu were cut off and given to Shu, Shu surely could not long endure—how much less when Shu gets the outer parts and we get the inner!
translations.idiomatic: If Wu falls, Shu will stand alone; if half of Wu were cut off and given to Shu, Shu surely could not long endure—how much less when Shu gets the outer parts and we get the inner!

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「人稱臣降而伐之，疑天下欲來者心，不若且受吳降而襲蜀之後也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "When a man declares himself a subject and submits, yet we attack him, we will make those throughout the empire who wish to come doubt their hearts—it is better for now to accept Wu's surrender and strike Shu afterward.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "When a man declares himself a subject and submits, yet we attack him, we will make those throughout the empire who wish to come doubt their hearts—it is better for now to accept Wu's surrender and strike Shu afterward.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「蜀遠吳近，又聞中國伐之，便還軍，不能止也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Shu is far and Wu is near; when they hear the Central State is attacking, they will at once withdraw their armies—we cannot stop them.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Shu is far and Wu is near; when they hear the Central State is attacking, they will at once withdraw their armies—we cannot stop them.

sentences.zh: 今備已怒，興兵擊吳，聞我伐吳，知吳必亡，將喜而進與我爭割吳地，必不改計抑怒救吳也。

translations.literal: Now Bei is already angered and has raised troops to attack Wu; when he hears we are attacking Wu, knowing Wu will surely perish, he will rejoice and advance to contend with us in carving up Wu's territory—he surely will not change his plan and suppress his anger to rescue Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Bei is already in a rage and has mobilized to strike Wu. Once he hears we are attacking Wu and knows Wu is doomed, he will press forward with joy to vie with us for a share of Wu's lands—he will surely not change course, swallow his fury, and come to Wu's rescue.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，遂受吳降。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not listen and thereupon accepted Wu's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor would not heed this advice and proceeded to accept Wu's surrender.

sentences.zh: 于禁鬚髮皓白，形容憔悴，見帝，泣涕頓首。

translations.literal: Yu Jin's beard and hair were white as snow; his appearance was haggard; seeing the Emperor, he wept and knocked his head to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin's hair and beard had turned snow-white, his face gaunt and worn; when he appeared before the Emperor he wept and prostrated himself in the dust.

sentences.zh: 帝慰喻以荀林父、孟明視故事，拜安遠將軍，令北詣鄴謁高陵。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and instructed him with the precedents of Xun Linfu and Meng Mingshi, appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distant, and ordered him north to Ye to pay respects at the Gaoling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor consoled him with the precedents of Xun Linfu and Meng Mingshi—generals who had failed yet been restored to grace—appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distant, and sent him north to Ye to pay homage at the Gaoling tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝使豫於陵屋畫關羽戰克、龐德憤怒、禁降服之狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor had painted in advance in the tomb-pavilion the scenes of Guan Yu's victorious battle, Pang De's angry defiance, and Jin's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had the tomb-pavilion painted in advance with scenes of Guan Yu's triumph, Pang De's defiant rage, and Jin's surrender.

sentences.zh: 禁見，慚恚發病死。

translations.literal: When Jin saw them, shame and resentment seized him and he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin saw the paintings, shame and fury overwhelmed him; he took ill and died.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：于禁將數萬眾，敗不能死，生降於敵，既而復歸。

translations.literal: ::Your subject Guang says: Yu Jin commanded tens of thousands, yet when defeated could not die—he surrendered alive to the enemy, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: ::Your subject Guang observes: Yu Jin commanded tens of thousands, yet when defeated he could not bring himself to die—he surrendered alive to the enemy, and then came home again.

sentences.zh: 文帝廢之可也，殺之可也，乃畫陵屋以辱之，斯為不君矣！

translations.literal: Emperor Wen might have dismissed him, or killed him—yet instead he painted them in the tomb-pavilion to humiliate him; this was not the conduct of a ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen might have dismissed him or put him to death; instead he had the tomb-pavilion painted to humiliate him—this was unworthy of a sovereign!

sentences.zh: 16丁巳，遣太常邢貞奉策即拜孫權為吳王，加九錫。

translations.literal: 16. On day dingsi, dispatched Grand Master of Ceremonies Xing Zhen bearing the edict to invest Sun Quan as King of Wu, adding the Nine Bestowments.
translations.idiomatic: 16. On the day dingsi, the Emperor dispatched Grand Master of Ceremonies Xing Zhen bearing an edict to invest Sun Quan as King of Wu, granting the Nine Bestowments.

sentences.zh: 劉曄曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Liu Ye said: "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye said: "This must not be done.

sentences.zh: 先帝征伐天下，十兼其八，威震海內；

translations.literal: The late Emperor campaigned across the empire and united nine parts in ten; his awe shook the seas.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor campaigned across the empire and united nine parts in ten; his majesty shook the seas.

sentences.zh: 陛下受禪即真，德合天地，聲暨四遠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the abdication and took the throne; your virtue matches Heaven and Earth, your renown reaches the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the abdication and ascended the throne; your virtue matches Heaven and Earth, your fame reaches the four corners of the earth.

sentences.zh: 權雖有雄才，故漢票騎帆軍、南昌侯耳，官輕勢卑。

translations.literal: Quan may have heroic talent, but he is merely the former Han Cavalry General and Marquis of Nanchang—his office is light in rank and low in standing.
translations.idiomatic: Quan may have heroic talent, but he is merely the former Han Cavalry General and Marquis of Nanchang—a title light in rank and low in prestige.

sentences.zh: 士民有畏中國心，不可強迫與成所謀也。

translations.literal: The gentry and common people still fear the Central State in their hearts; we cannot forcibly press them into whatever scheme they propose.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common people still hold the Central State in awe; we cannot forcibly press them into whatever design they propose.

sentences.zh: 不得已受其降，可進其將軍號，封十萬戶侯，不可即以為王也。

translations.literal: Being unable to do otherwise, we may accept his surrender—but only advance his general's title and enfeoff him as a marquis of one hundred thousand households; we must not at once make him a king.
translations.idiomatic: If we must accept his surrender, we may advance his general's title and enfeoff him as a marquis of one hundred thousand households—but we must not at once make him a king.

sentences.zh: 夫王位去天子一階耳，其禮秩服御相亂也。

translations.literal: The position of king is only one step below the Son of Heaven; its rites, rank, dress, and accoutrements become confused with the imperial.
translations.idiomatic: The rank of king stands only one step below the Son of Heaven; its rites, precedence, dress, and regalia blur the line with the imperial.

sentences.zh: 彼直為侯，江南士民未有君臣之分。

translations.literal: Were he merely a marquis, the gentry and people of Jiangnan would still lack the distinction of lord and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Were he merely a marquis, the gentry and people of Jiangnan would still lack a settled bond of lord and subject.

sentences.zh: 我信其偽降，就封殖之，崇其位號，定其君臣，是為虎傅翼也。

translations.literal: We credit his feigned surrender and proceed to ennoble him, elevate his title and rank, and fix his status as lord and subject—is this not giving wings to a tiger?
translations.idiomatic: We credit his feigned surrender, proceed to ennoble him, elevate his title and rank, and fix his status as sovereign and subject—is this not giving wings to a tiger?

sentences.zh: 權既受王位，卻蜀兵之後，外盡禮以事中國，使其國內皆聞，內為無禮以怒陛下；

translations.literal: Once Quan receives the kingship, he will repel Shu's forces from behind; outwardly he will exhaust every courtesy in serving the Central State, letting all within his state hear of it, while inwardly acting without courtesy to provoke Your Majesty—
translations.idiomatic: Once Quan receives the kingship, he will repel Shu's forces from behind; outwardly he will exhaust every courtesy in serving the Central State, letting all within his realm hear of it, while inwardly acting without courtesy to provoke Your Majesty—

sentences.zh: 陛下赫然發怒，興兵討之，乃徐告其民曰：『我委身事中國，不愛珍貨重寶，隨時貢獻，不敢失臣禮，而無故伐我，必欲殘我國家，俘我人民認為僕妾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, suddenly enraged, raises troops to chastise him; then at leisure he will tell his people: 'I have devoted myself to serving the Central State, not sparing precious treasures or rare goods, always presenting tribute and never failing in a subject's duty—yet for no reason you attack us, you must mean to destroy our state, capture our people, and make them your slaves and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, suddenly enraged, will raise troops to chastise him; then at leisure he will tell his people: 'I have devoted myself to serving the Central State, not sparing precious treasures or rare goods, always presenting tribute and never failing in a subject's duty—yet for no reason you attack us, you must mean to destroy our state, capture our people, and make them your slaves and concubines.

sentences.zh: 』吳民無緣不信其言也。

translations.literal: ' The people of Wu would have no reason not to believe his words.
translations.idiomatic: ' The people of Wu would have no reason not to believe his words.

sentences.zh: 信其言而感怒，上下同心，戰加十倍矣。

translations.literal: Believing his words and stirred to anger, above and below united—their fighting strength would increase tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his words and stirred to anger, above and below united—their fighting strength would increase tenfold.

sentences.zh: 」又不聽。

translations.literal: " Again he was not listened to.
translations.idiomatic: " Again the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 諸將以吳內附，意皆縱緩，獨征南大將軍夏侯尚益修攻守之備。

translations.literal: The generals, seeing Wu submit from within, all relaxed their guard; only the General Who Subdues the South, Xiahou Shang, further strengthened offensive and defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, seeing Wu submit from within, all relaxed their guard; only General Who Subdues the South Xiahou Shang further strengthened offensive and defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 山陽曹偉，素有才名，聞吳稱籓，以白衣與吳王交書求賂，欲以交結京師，帝聞而誅之。

translations.literal: Cao Wei of Shanyang, famed for talent, hearing Wu declared itself a vassal state, as a commoner exchanged letters with the King of Wu seeking bribes, intending to establish contacts in the capital; the Emperor hearing of this executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei of Shanyang, famed for talent, hearing that Wu had declared itself a vassal state, as a commoner exchanged letters with the King of Wu seeking bribes, intending to cultivate contacts in the capital; when the Emperor heard of this he had him executed.

sentences.zh: 17吳又城武昌。

translations.literal: 17. Wu again fortified Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 17. Wu again fortified Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 18初，帝欲以楊彪為太尉，彪辭曰：「嘗為漢朝三公，值世衰亂，不能立尺寸之益，若復為魏臣，於國之選，亦不為榮也。

translations.literal: 18. Earlier, the Emperor wished to appoint Yang Biao as Grand Commandant; Biao declined, saying: "I once served the Han dynasty as one of the Three Ducal Ministers; when the age declined into chaos I could not establish benefit even the size of an inch—if I now become a minister of Wei again, in the state's selection it would not be glory either.
translations.idiomatic: 18. Earlier, the Emperor wished to appoint Yang Biao as Grand Commandant; Biao declined, saying: "I once served the Han dynasty as one of the Three Ducal Ministers; when the age declined into chaos I could not achieve even the slightest good—if I now become a minister of Wei again, in the state's eyes it would be no honor either.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then desisted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己亥，公卿朝朔旦，並引彪，待以客禮。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jihai, the dukes and ministers attended the morning audience on the new-moon day, all together receiving Yang Biao, treating him with guest's courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, on the day jihai, the dukes and ministers attended the new-moon audience and all received Yang Biao, treating him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 賜延年杖、馮几，使著布單衣、皮弁以見；

translations.literal: He was granted the staff of longevity and a folding armrest, and made to appear dressed in a cloth single garment and a leather cap;
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the staff of longevity and a folding armrest, and made to appear dressed in a plain cloth robe and a leather cap;

sentences.zh: 拜光祿大夫，秩中二千石；

translations.literal: appointed Grand Master of Splendor, with salary rank of two thousand shi;
translations.idiomatic: appointed him Grand Master of Splendor, with salary rank of two thousand shi;

sentences.zh: 朝見，位次三公；

translations.literal: at court audiences, his seat was after the Three Ducal Ministers;
translations.idiomatic: at court audiences, his seat was ranked after the Three Ducal Ministers;

sentences.zh: 又令門施行馬，置吏卒，以優崇之。

translations.literal: furthermore his gate was given the privilege of post-horses, and officials and soldiers were stationed there to honor and exalt him.
translations.idiomatic: furthermore his gate was granted the privilege of post-horses, and officials and soldiers were stationed there to honor and exalt him.

sentences.zh: 年八十四而卒。

translations.literal: At age eighty-four he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 19以穀貴，罷五銖錢。

translations.literal: 19. Because grain was dear, the five-zhu coin was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 19. Because grain was dear, the five-zhu coin was abolished.

sentences.zh: 20涼州盧水胡治元多等反，河西大擾。

translations.literal: 20. Zhiyuan Duo and others of the Lushui Hu in Liangzhou rebelled; west of the Yellow River there was great disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: 20. Zhiyuan Duo and others of the Lushui Hu in Liangzhou rebelled, and the region west of the Yellow River was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝召鄒岐還，以京兆尹張既為涼州刺史，遣護軍夏侯儒、將軍費曜等繼其後。

translations.literal: The Emperor recalled Zou Qi and appointed the Governor of Jingzhao, Zhang Ji, as Governor of Liangzhou, dispatching Protector of the Army Xiahou Ru and General Fei Yao and others to follow after.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Zou Qi and appointed Zhang Ji, Governor of Jingzhao, as Governor of Liangzhou, dispatching Protector of the Army Xiahou Ru, General Fei Yao, and others to follow after.

sentences.zh: 胡七千餘騎逆拒既於鸇陰口，既揚聲軍從鸇陰，乃潛由且次出武威。

translations.literal: Over seven thousand Hu horsemen met Ji at Zhuanyinkou to resist; Ji publicly announced the army would follow Zhuanyin, then secretly marched out from Qieci toward Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven thousand Hu horsemen met Ji at Zhuanyinkou to resist; Ji publicly announced that his army would advance by way of Zhuanyin, then secretly marched out from Qieci toward Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 胡以為神，引還顯美。

translations.literal: The Hu thought this divine and withdrew to Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu took this for divine intervention and withdrew to Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 既已據武威，曜乃至，儒等猶未達。

translations.literal: Ji had already seized Wuwei when Yao arrived; Ru and the others had not yet reached there.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had already seized Wuwei when Yao arrived; Ru and the others had not yet reached there.

sentences.zh: 既勞賜將士，欲進軍擊胡，諸將皆曰：「士卒疲倦，虜眾氣銳，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: Ji rewarded the officers and soldiers and wished to advance and attack the Hu; the generals all said: "The soldiers are weary, the enemy masses are keen in spirit—hard to contend with their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rewarded the officers and soldiers and wished to advance and attack the Hu; the generals all said: "The soldiers are weary, the enemy masses are keen in spirit—hard to contend with their edge.

sentences.zh: 」既曰：「今軍無見糧，當因敵為資。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "Now the army has no visible grain—we must take the enemy as our supply.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji said: "Now the army has no visible grain—we must take the enemy as our supply.

sentences.zh: 若虜見兵合，退依深山，追之則道險窮餓，兵還則出候寇鈔，如此，兵不得解，所謂一日縱敵，患在數世也。

translations.literal: If the enemy see our forces unite, they will retreat into deep mountains; pursue them and the roads are perilous and we will be starved; if the army returns they will come out to watch and plunder—thus the army cannot be released; this is what is called 'let the enemy go for a day, and the disaster lasts for generations.'
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy see our forces unite, they will retreat into the deep mountains; pursue them and the roads are perilous and we will be starved; if the army returns they will come out to watch and plunder—thus the army cannot be released. This is what is called 'let the enemy go for a day, and the disaster lasts for generations.'

sentences.zh: 」遂前軍顯美。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the army advanced to Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the army advanced to Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，胡騎數千，因大風欲放火燒營，將士皆恐。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, several thousand Hu horsemen, taking advantage of a strong wind, intended to set fire and burn the camp; officers and soldiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, several thousand Hu horsemen, taking advantage of a strong wind, intended to set fire and burn the camp; officers and soldiers were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 既夜藏精卒三千人為伏，使參軍成公英督千餘騎挑戰，敕使陽退。

translations.literal: By night Ji hid three thousand picked soldiers as an ambush, had Adjunct Cheng Gongying lead over a thousand horsemen to challenge battle, and ordered a feigned retreat.
translations.idiomatic: By night Ji hid three thousand picked soldiers in ambush, had Adjunct Cheng Gongying lead over a thousand horsemen to offer battle, and ordered a feigned retreat.

sentences.zh: 胡果爭奔之，因發伏截其後，首尾進擊，大破之，斬首獲生以萬數，河西悉平。

translations.literal: The Hu indeed raced after them in competition; then the ambush was sprung to cut off their rear, attacking from fore and aft; they were utterly routed—heads cut and captives taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and all west of the river was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu indeed raced after them in competition; then the ambush was sprung to cut off their rear, attacking from fore and aft; they were utterly routed—heads cut and captives taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and all west of the river was pacified.

sentences.zh: 後西平麴光反，殺其郡守。

translations.literal: Later Qu Guang of Xiping rebelled and killed the prefect of his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qu Guang of Xiping rebelled and killed the prefect of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲擊之，既曰：「唯光等造反，郡人未必悉同。

translations.literal: The generals wished to attack; Ji said: "Only Guang and his ilk rebel—the people of the commandery are not necessarily all alike.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wished to attack; Ji said: "Only Guang and his ilk rebel—the people of the commandery are not necessarily all alike.

sentences.zh: 若便以軍臨之，吏民、羌、胡必謂國家不別是非，更使皆相持著，此為虎傅翼也。

translations.literal: If we at once bring the army down on them, officials and people, Qiang, and Hu will all say the state makes no distinction between right and wrong, and each will hold fast in mutual resistance—this is giving wings to a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: If we at once bring the army down on them, officials and people, Qiang, and Hu will all say the state makes no distinction between right and wrong, and each will hold fast in mutual resistance—this is giving wings to a tiger.

sentences.zh: 光等欲以羌、胡為援，今先使羌、胡鈔擊，重其賞募，所虜獲者，皆以畀之。

translations.literal: Guang and his ilk wish to use the Qiang and Hu as support; now first send the Qiang and Hu to raid and attack, with heavy bounty rewards—whatever they capture and take, all is given to them.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and his ilk wish to use the Qiang and Hu as support; now first send the Qiang and Hu to raid and attack, with heavy bounty rewards—whatever they capture and take, all is given to them.

sentences.zh: 外沮其勢，內離其交，必不戰而定。

translations.literal: Externally check their momentum, internally sunder their alliances—surely without battle it will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Externally check their momentum, internally sunder their alliances—surely without battle it will be settled.

sentences.zh: 」乃移檄告諭諸羌，為光等所詿誤者原之，能斬賊帥送首者當加封賞。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict was moved and circulated to notify the various Qiang: those misled by Guang and his ilk are forgiven; whoever can cut off the rebel chieftain and deliver his head will receive enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon a proclamation was circulated to notify the various Qiang: those misled by Guang and his ilk were forgiven; whoever could cut off the rebel chieftain and deliver his head would receive enfeoffment and reward.

sentences.zh: 於是光部黨斬送光首，其餘皆安堵如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guang's partisans cut off and delivered Guang's head; the rest all dwelled in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Guang's partisans cut off and delivered Guang's head; the rest all dwelled in peace as before.

sentences.zh: 21邢貞至吳，吳人以為宜稱上將軍、九州伯，不當受魏封。

translations.literal: 21. Xing Zhen arrived in Wu; the men of Wu thought he ought to style himself General-in-Chief and Lord of the Nine Provinces, and should not accept Wei enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: 21. When Xing Zhen arrived in Wu, the men of Wu thought Sun Quan ought to style himself General-in-Chief and Lord of the Nine Provinces, and should not accept Wei's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 吳王曰：「九州伯，於古未聞也。

translations.literal: The King of Wu said: "Lord of the Nine Provinces—never heard of in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu said: "Lord of the Nine Provinces—never heard of in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 昔沛公亦受項羽封為漢王，蓋時宜耳，復何損邪！

translations.literal: In old days Lord Pei also received investiture from Xiang Yu as King of Han—this was merely suited to the times; what harm in it again!
translations.idiomatic: In old days the Lord of Pei also received investiture from Xiang Yu as King of Han—this was merely suited to the times; what harm could there be in it!

sentences.zh: 」遂受之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he accepted it.

sentences.zh: 吳王出都亭候邢貞，貞入門，不下車。

translations.literal: The King of Wu went out to the capital pavilion to await Xing Zhen; when Zhen entered the gate he did not alight from his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu went out to the capital pavilion to await Xing Zhen; when Zhen entered the gate he did not alight from his carriage.

sentences.zh: 張昭謂貞曰：「夫禮無不敬，法無不行。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao said to Zhen: "In ritual nothing is not reverent; in law nothing is not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao said to Zhen: "In ritual nothing is without reverence; in law nothing goes unenforced.

sentences.zh: 而君敢自尊大，豈以江南寡弱，無方寸之刃故乎！

translations.literal: Yet you dare to make yourself lofty and great—is it because south of the Yangtze is weak and small, without a blade an inch in size!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you dare to hold yourself above others—is it because the south of the Yangtze is weak and small, without so much as a blade an inch long!

sentences.zh: 」貞即遽下車。

translations.literal: " Zhen at once hurried down from his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen at once hurried down from his carriage.

sentences.zh: 中郎將琅邪徐盛忿憤，顧謂同列曰：「盛等不能奮身出命，為國家並許、洛，吞巴、蜀，而令吾君與貞盟，不亦辱乎！

translations.literal: Central Palace Gentleman Langye Xu Sheng, resentful and indignant, turned to his fellows and said: "We could not exert our bodies and give our lives, unite Xu and Luo for the state, swallow Ba and Shu—and now we make our lord ally with Zhen—is this not shame!
translations.idiomatic: Central Palace Gentleman Xu Sheng of Langye, resentful and indignant, turned to his fellows and said: "We could not exert ourselves and give our lives, unite Xu and Luo for the state, swallow Ba and Shu—and now we make our lord ally with Zhen—is this not shame!

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣橫流。

translations.literal: " Then tears flowed across his face.
translations.idiomatic: " Then tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 貞聞之，謂其徒曰：「江東將相如此，非久下人者也。

translations.literal: Zhen hearing this said to his followers: "Generals and ministers east of the river like this—they will not long be men's inferiors.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen heard this he said to his followers: "Generals and ministers east of the river like this—they will not long remain another's inferiors.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「吳王何等主也？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "What sort of ruler is the King of Wu?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "What sort of ruler is the King of Wu?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聰明、仁智、雄略之主也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "A ruler who is intelligent, benevolent, wise, and strategically farsighted.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "A ruler who is intelligent, benevolent, wise, and strategically farsighted.

sentences.zh: 」帝問其狀，對曰：「納魯肅於凡品，是其聰也；

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked for particulars; he replied: "Taking Lu Su from common rank—that was his intelligence;
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked for particulars; he replied: "Taking Lu Su from common rank—that was his intelligence;

sentences.zh: 拔呂蒙於行陳，是其明也；

translations.literal: promoting Lü Meng from the ranks—that was his discernment;
translations.idiomatic: promoting Lü Meng from the ranks—that was his discernment;

sentences.zh: 獲於禁而不害，是其仁也；

translations.literal: capturing Yu Jin yet not harming him—that was his benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: capturing Yu Jin yet not harming him—that was his benevolence;

sentences.zh: 取荊州兵不血刃，是其智也；

translations.literal: taking Jing Province without blades blooded—that was his wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: taking Jing Province without blades blooded—that was his wisdom;

sentences.zh: 據三州虎視於天下，是其雄也；

translations.literal: holding three provinces and glaring tiger-like at the empire—that was his heroism;
translations.idiomatic: holding three provinces and glaring tiger-like at the empire—that was his heroism;

sentences.zh: 屈身於陛下，是其略也。

translations.literal: bowing in submission to Your Majesty—that was his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: bowing in submission to Your Majesty—that was his strategy.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吳王頗知學乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Does the King of Wu know much of learning?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Does the King of Wu know much of learning?

sentences.zh: 」咨曰：「吳王浮江萬艘，帶甲百萬，任賢使能，志存經略，雖有餘閒，博覽書傳，歷史籍，采奇異，不效書生尋章摘句而已。

translations.literal: " Zhao Zi said: "The King of Wu has ten thousand vessels on the river, a million armored men, employs the worthy and uses the able, his intent fixed on statecraft and strategy—though he has leisure besides, he broadly reads books and transmissions, histories and records, gathers the strange and unusual—not merely imitating bookish men picking passages and culling phrases.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Zi said: "The King of Wu has ten thousand vessels on the river and a million armored men; he employs the worthy and uses the able, his intent fixed on statecraft and strategy. Though he has leisure besides, he broadly reads books and transmissions, histories and records, and gathers the strange and unusual—not merely imitating bookish men who pick passages and cull phrases."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吳可征否？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Can Wu be attacked?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Can Wu be attacked?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「大國有征伐之兵，小國有備御之固。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Great states have troops for campaigning; small states have defenses that are firm.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Great states have troops for campaigning; small states have defenses that are firm.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吳難魏乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Is Wu a match for Wei?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Is Wu a match for Wei?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「帶甲百萬，江、漢為池，何難之有！

translations.literal: " He replied: "With a million armored men, the Yangtze and Han as moats—what difficulty is there!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "With a million armored men and the Yangtze and Han as moats—what difficulty could there be!"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吳如大夫者幾人？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "How many men in Wu are like you, a grandee?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "How many men in Wu are like you, a grandee?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聰明特達者，八九十人；

translations.literal: " He replied: "Those outstanding in intelligence and penetrating insight—eighty or ninety men;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Those outstanding in intelligence and penetrating insight—eighty or ninety men;

sentences.zh: 如臣之比，車載斗量，不可勝數。

translations.literal: men like myself—cartloads and bushel-measures, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: men like myself—cartloads and bushel-measures, beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使求雀頭香、大貝、明珠、象牙、犀角、玳瑁、孔雀、翡翠、鬥鴨、長鳴雞於吳。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to request from Wu sparrow-head incense, great shells, luminous pearls, ivory, rhinoceros horn, tortoiseshell, peacocks, kingfishers, fighting ducks, and long-crowing cocks.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent envoys to request from Wu sparrow-head incense, great shells, luminous pearls, ivory, rhinoceros horn, tortoiseshell, peacocks, kingfishers, fighting ducks, and long-crowing cocks.

sentences.zh: 吳群臣曰：「荊、揚二州，貢有常典。

translations.literal: The ministers of Wu said: "The two provinces Jing and Yang have fixed tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of Wu said: "The two provinces Jing and Yang have fixed tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 魏所求珍玩之物，非禮也，宜勿與。

translations.literal: What Wei requests are precious playthings—not according to ritual; we ought not give them.
translations.idiomatic: What Wei requests are precious playthings—not according to ritual; we ought not give them.

sentences.zh: 」吳王曰：「方有事於西北，江表元元，恃主為命。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu said: "We are presently engaged with affairs in the northwest; the common folk beyond the river all rely on me for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Wu said: "We are presently engaged with affairs in the northwest; the common folk beyond the river all rely on me for their lives.

sentences.zh: 彼所求者，於我瓦石耳，孤何惜焉！

translations.literal: What they seek from us are but tiles and stones to us—why should I begrudge them!
translations.idiomatic: What they seek from us are but tiles and stones to us—why should I begrudge them!

sentences.zh: 且彼在諒闇之中，而所求若此，寧可與言禮哉！

translations.literal: Moreover they are in the mourning solitude after bereavement, yet ask for things like this—can one discuss ritual with them!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they are in mourning after bereavement, yet ask for things like this—can one discuss ritual with them!

sentences.zh: 」皆具以與之。

translations.literal: " All were fully supplied and given.
translations.idiomatic: " All were fully supplied and given.

sentences.zh: 22吳王以其子登為太子，妙選師友，以南郡太守諸葛瑾之子恪、綏遠將軍張昭之子休、大理吳郡顧雍之子譚、偏將軍廬江陳武之子表皆為中庶子，入講詩書，出從騎射，謂之四友。

translations.literal: 22. The King of Wu made his son Deng crown prince, finely selected teachers and companions—making Zhuge Ke son of Grand Administrator of Nanjun Zhuge Jin, Sun Xiu son of General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao, Gu Tan son of Grand Judge of Wujun Gu Yong, and Chen Biao son of Adjunct General of Lujiang Chen Wu all Supernumerary Palace Attendants, entering to lecture on Poetry and Documents, going out to follow in horsemanship and archery—calling them the Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: 22. The King of Wu made his son Deng crown prince and finely selected teachers and companions—making Zhuge Ke, son of Grand Administrator of Nanjun Zhuge Jin; Sun Xiu, son of General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao; Gu Tan, son of Grand Judge of Wujun Gu Yong; and Chen Biao, son of Adjunct General of Lujiang Chen Wu all Supernumerary Palace Attendants. They entered to lecture on the Poetry and Documents and went out to follow in horsemanship and archery—he called them the Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 登接待僚屬，略用布衣之禮。

translations.literal: Deng in receiving and attending to subordinates generally used the courtesies of the plain-clothed.
translations.idiomatic: In receiving and attending to subordinates, Deng generally used the courtesies of a plain-clothed gentleman.

translations.idiomatic: 23. In the twelfth month, the Emperor went on an eastern tour.

translations.literal: 24. The Emperor wished to enfeoff the Prince of Wu, Deng, as a Marquis of Ten Thousand Households; the King of Wu, considering Deng still young, submitted a memorial declining to accept;
translations.idiomatic: 24. The Emperor wished to enfeoff Sun Deng, prince of Wu, as a marquis of ten thousand households; the King of Wu, considering Deng still too young, submitted a memorial declining the honor;
