translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked: "Does Wu resent Wei's turning eastward?

sentences.zh: 」珩曰：「不嫌。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "No resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " Heng said: "No resentment.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「何以？

translations.literal: " He said: "Why?
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "Why?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「信恃舊盟，言歸於好，是以不嫌；

translations.literal: " He said: "Trusting and relying on the old alliance, speaking of return to good relations—for this reason no resentment;
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "We trust in the old alliance and speak of restoring good relations, and for that reason feel no resentment;

sentences.zh: 若魏渝盟，自有豫備。

translations.literal: if Wei violates the alliance, naturally there are preparations.
translations.idiomatic: if Wei violates the alliance, we naturally have our preparations in place.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「聞太子當來，寧然乎？

translations.literal: " He asked again: "I hear the crown prince is to come—is it so?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again: "I hear the crown prince is to come—is it so?

sentences.zh: 」珩曰：「臣在東朝，朝不坐，宴不與，若此之議，無所聞也。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "Your subject in the Eastern Court—does not sit at court sessions, does not join at banquets; such talk I have heard nothing of.
translations.idiomatic: " Heng said: "When I was at the Eastern Court, I did not sit in at court sessions or join at banquets; I have heard nothing of such talk.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor approved of this.

sentences.zh: 吳王於武昌臨釣臺飲酒，大醉，使人以水灑群臣曰：「今日酣飲，惟醉墮台中，乃當止耳！

translations.literal: The King of Wu at Wuchang, at the Fishing Terrace drinking wine, greatly drunk, sent men to sprinkle water on the assembled ministers and said: "Today's deep drinking—only when drunk and fallen into the terrace shall we stop!
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang the King of Wu held wine at the Fishing Terrace until he was thoroughly drunk; he had water sprinkled on the assembled ministers and said: "Today we drink deep—only when one is drunk enough to fall from this terrace shall we stop!"

sentences.zh: 」張昭正色不言，出外，車中坐。

translations.literal: " Zhang Zhao with stern countenance spoke not, went outside, sat in his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Zhao kept a stern face and said nothing; he went outside and sat in his carriage.

sentences.zh: 王遣人呼昭還入，謂曰：「為共作樂耳，公何為怒乎？

translations.literal: The King sent men to summon Zhao back in, saying: "It is merely to share merriment—why is the Lord angry?
translations.idiomatic: The King sent men to summon Zhao back in and said: "We are only sharing merriment together—why so angry, my lord?

sentences.zh: 」昭對曰：「昔紂為糟丘酒池，長夜之飲，當時亦以為榮，不以為惡也。

translations.literal: " Zhao replied: "Formerly Zhou of Shang made the wine-mound and wine-pool, the all-night drinking—at the time it was also regarded as glory, not regarded as evil.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao replied: "In olden days King Zhou of Shang built the wine-mound and wine-pool and held all-night drinking bouts; at the time men thought it glorious and did not think it wicked.

sentences.zh: 」王默然慚，遂罷酒。

translations.literal: " The King silently ashamed, thereupon stopped the wine.
translations.idiomatic: " The King fell silent in shame and stopped the drinking.

sentences.zh: 吳王與群臣飲，自起行酒，虞翻伏地，陽醉不持；

translations.literal: The King of Wu with assembled ministers drinking, himself rose to offer wine; Yu Fan prostrated on the ground, feigned drunkenness and did not take it;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu was drinking with his ministers and rose to offer wine in turn; Yu Fan prostrated himself and feigned drunkenness, refusing the cup;

sentences.zh: 王去，翻起坐。

translations.literal: the King departed, Fan rose and sat.
translations.idiomatic: when the King had moved on, Fan rose and sat up.

sentences.zh: 王大怒，手劍欲擊之，侍坐者莫不惶遽。

translations.literal: The King greatly angered, sword in hand wished to strike him; those seated in attendance none not alarmed and flustered.
translations.idiomatic: The King flew into a rage, drew his sword and was about to strike him; everyone present was struck with alarm.

sentences.zh: 惟大司農劉基起抱王，諫曰：「大王以三爵之後，手殺善士，雖翻有罪，天下孰知之！

translations.literal: Only Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu Ji rose and embraced the King, remonstrating: "Great King, after three cups of wine, personally killing a good officer—even if Fan has guilt, who in the empire would know it!
translations.idiomatic: Only Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu Ji rose and held the King back, remonstrating: "Great King, to personally kill a good officer after the third cup—even if Fan is guilty, who in the empire would know the truth of it!

sentences.zh: 且大王以能容賢蓄眾，故海內望風；

translations.literal: Moreover the Great King, by being able to embrace the worthy and gather the multitude—therefore within the four seas men look to your wind;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it is because you can embrace the worthy and gather men about you that the empire looks to you with hope;

sentences.zh: 今一朝棄之，可乎！

translations.literal: now in one morning to abandon this—can it be!
translations.idiomatic: to cast that aside in a single morning—how can that be right!

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「曹孟德尚殺孔文舉，孤於虞翻何有哉！

translations.literal: " The King said: "Lord Cao Mengde yet killed Kong Wenju—what is there in Yu Fan for me!
translations.idiomatic: " The King said: "Even Cao Mengde killed Kong Wenju—what is Yu Fan to me!

sentences.zh: 」基曰：「孟德輕害士人，天下非之。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "Mengde lightly harmed scholar-officers; the empire condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji said: "Mengde killed scholar-officers lightly, and the empire condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 大王躬行德義，欲與堯、舜比隆，何得自喻於彼乎？

translations.literal: The Great King personally practices virtue and righteousness, wishing to match Yao and Shun in exaltation—how can one compare oneself to him!
translations.idiomatic: You personally practice virtue and righteousness and aspire to rank with Yao and Shun—how can you compare yourself to him!

sentences.zh: 」翻由是得免。

translations.literal: " Fan thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Fan thereby escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 王因敕左右：「自今酒後言殺，皆不得殺。

translations.literal: The King thereby ordered those at his side: "From now on, after wine when kill is spoken, none may be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The King thereupon ordered those at his side: "From now on, whenever anyone speaks of killing after wine, no one is to be killed."

sentences.zh: 」基，繇之子。

translations.literal: " Ji was the son of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji was the son of Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 25初，太祖既克蹋頓，而烏桓浸衰，鮮卑大人步度根、軻比能、素利、彌加、厥機等因閻柔上貢獻，求通市，太祖皆表寵以為王。

translations.literal: 25. At the beginning, the Grand Ancestor having defeated Tadun, the Wuhuan gradually declined; Xianbei great chiefs Budugen, Kebineng, Suli, Mijia, Jueji and others through Yan Rou submitted tribute, sought to open markets; the Grand Ancestor all memorialized to ennoble them as kings.
translations.idiomatic: 25. At the outset, after the Grand Ancestor had defeated Tadun, the Wuhuan gradually declined; the Xianbei chieftains Budugen, Kebineng, Suli, Mijia, Jueji, and others, through Yan Rou, submitted tribute and sought to open trade. The Grand Ancestor memorialized the throne to ennoble them all as kings.

sentences.zh: 軻比能本小種鮮卑，以勇健廉平為眾所服，由是能威制餘部，最為強盛。

translations.literal: Kebineng originally of the lesser Xianbei clans, by courage, vigor, integrity and fairness was respected by the multitude; thereby able to awe and control the remaining tribes, most powerful and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Kebineng came from a lesser Xianbei clan; his courage, vigor, integrity, and fairness won the people's respect, and he was thus able to awe and control the other tribes, becoming the most powerful of them all.

sentences.zh: 自雲中、五原以東抵遼水，皆為鮮卑庭，軻比能與素利、彌加割地統御，各有分界。

translations.literal: From Yunzhong and Wuyuan east to the Liao River, all was Xianbei territory; Kebineng with Suli and Mijia divided lands and governed, each having boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: From Yunzhong and Wuyuan eastward to the Liao River all became Xianbei domain; Kebineng, Suli, and Mijia divided the land among themselves to govern, each with his own borders.

sentences.zh: 軻比能部落近塞，中國人多亡叛歸之；

translations.literal: Kebineng's tribes near the border forts; many Chinese men fled and rebelled to join him;
translations.idiomatic: Kebineng's tribes lay near the border forts, and many Chinese fled or defected to join him;

sentences.zh: 素利等在遼西、右北平、漁陽塞外，道遠，故不為邊患。

translations.literal: Suli and the others beyond the forts of Liaoxi, Right Beiping, and Yuyang—the roads far; therefore not border troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Suli and the others lay beyond the border forts of Liaoxi, Right Beiping, and Yuyang; the distance was great, so they posed no border threat.

sentences.zh: 帝以平虜校尉牽招為護鮮卑校尉，南陽太守田豫為護烏桓校尉，使鎮撫之。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians Qian Zhao Protector Colonel of the Xianbei, Grand Administrator of Nanyang Tian Yu Protector Colonel of the Wuhuan, sending them to guard and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians Qian Zhao as Protector Colonel of the Xianbei and Grand Administrator of Nanyang Tian Yu as Protector Colonel of the Wuhuan, and sent them to guard and pacify the tribes.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，丙寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, on the day Bingyin the new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, on the first day of the first month (the day Bingyin), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 2庚午，帝行如許昌。

translations.literal: 2. On the day Gengwu, the Emperor proceeded to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 2. On the day Gengwu, the Emperor proceeded to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 3詔曰：「今之計、孝，古之貢士也；

translations.literal: 3. An edict said: "Today's provincial and filial recommendation system is the ancient tribute-officer system;
translations.idiomatic: 3. An edict stated: "Today's provincial recommendation and filial-piety selection are the ancient tribute-officer system;

sentences.zh: 若限年然後取士，是呂尚、周晉不顯於前世也。

translations.literal: if by limiting age and then selecting officers, then Lü Shang and Zhou Jin would not have been distinguished in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: if selection were limited by age, then Lü Shang and Zhou Jin would never have risen to distinction in former ages.

sentences.zh: 其令郡國所選，勿拘老幼；

translations.literal: Accordingly order the commanderies and states in selection not to be bound by old and young;
translations.idiomatic: Let the commanderies and feudatories in making selections not be restricted by age;

sentences.zh: 儒通經術，吏達文法，到皆試用。

translations.literal: Confucians mastering the classics and arts, officers skilled in statutes and law—upon arrival all shall be tried in employment.
translations.idiomatic: those who master the classics and the rites and those skilled in law and administration shall all, upon arrival, be given trial appointments.

sentences.zh: 有司糾故不以實者。

translations.literal: the responsible offices shall investigate and report those who do not act according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: Responsible offices shall investigate and punish those who fail to recommend men of genuine merit.

sentences.zh: 4二月，鄯善、龜茲、于闐王各遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: 4. Second month, the kings of Shanshan, Kucha, and Khotan each sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In the second month, the kings of Shanshan, Kucha, and Khotan each sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 是後西域復通，置戊己校尉。

translations.literal: After this the Western Regions were again connected; the Wuji Colonel was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter contact with the Western Regions was restored, and the Wuji Colonel was installed.

sentences.zh: 5漢主自秭歸將進擊吳，治中從事黃權諫曰：「吳人悍戰，而水軍沿流，進易退難。

translations.literal: 5. The Han Lord from Zigui was about to advance and attack Wu; Administrator Attendant Huang Quan remonstrated: "Wu men fight fiercely, and with the navy following the stream, advance is easy, retreat difficult.
translations.idiomatic: 5. The Han ruler was about to advance from Zigui to attack Wu. Administrator-attendant Huang Quan remonstrated: "The Wu men fight fiercely, and with the navy moving downstream, advance is easy but retreat will be hard.

sentences.zh: 臣請為先驅以當寇，陛下宜為後鎮。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to serve as vanguard to meet the enemy; Your Majesty should serve as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to serve as vanguard and meet the enemy; Your Majesty should hold the rear."

sentences.zh: 」漢主不從，以權為鎮北將軍，使督江北諸軍；

translations.literal: " The Han Lord did not follow; made Quan General Who Pacifies the North, sent him to supervise all armies north of the river;
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler refused and instead made Huang Quan General Who Pacifies the North, assigning him to command all forces north of the Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 自率諸將，自江南緣山截嶺，軍於夷道猇亭。

translations.literal: himself leading the generals, from south of the river along mountains cutting ridges, encamped at Yidao and Xiaoting.
translations.idiomatic: while he personally led his generals south of the Yangtze along the mountain ridges, encamping at Yidao and Xiaoting.

sentences.zh: 吳將皆欲迎擊之。

translations.literal: Wu generals all wished to meet and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu generals all wished to meet them in battle.

sentences.zh: 陸遜曰：「備舉軍東下，銳氣始盛；

translations.literal: Lu Xun said: "Bei has raised the whole army eastward; keen spirit just flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said: "Liu Bei has marched his whole army east; their fighting spirit is at its peak;

sentences.zh: 且乘高守險，難可卒攻。

translations.literal: moreover occupying heights and guarding passes—hard to suddenly attack.
translations.idiomatic: they hold the heights and guard the passes, and cannot be taken in a hasty assault.

sentences.zh: 攻之縱下，猶難盡克，若有不利，損我太勢，非小故也。

translations.literal: Attack them even if it succeeds, still hard to fully overcome; if there is disadvantage, damage to our great momentum—not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Even if an attack should succeed, complete victory would still be hard to achieve; any setback would damage our momentum grievously.

sentences.zh: 今但且獎厲將士，廣施方略，以觀其變。

translations.literal: Now for the present only encourage and exhort officers and soldiers, broadly deploy stratagems, to observe their changes.
translations.idiomatic: For now, let us only encourage the troops, employ varied stratagems, and watch how matters develop.

sentences.zh: 若此間是平原曠野，當恐有顛沛交逐之憂；

translations.literal: If this region were open plain and vast field, one ought to fear concern of distress and mutual pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: If this were open country, we might fear being thrown into disorder in a running pursuit;

sentences.zh: 今緣山行軍，勢不得展，自當罷於木石之間，徐制其敝耳。

translations.literal: now along mountains marching armies, momentum cannot expand—they naturally will wear out among trees and rocks; slowly control their exhaustion, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: but marching along these mountain tracks, their forces cannot deploy; they will wear themselves out among the cliffs and boulders, and we can gradually overcome them at our leisure."

sentences.zh: 」諸將不解，以為遜畏之，各懷憤恨。

translations.literal: " The generals did not understand, considered Xun afraid of them, each harbored anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The generals did not understand and thought Lu Xun feared the enemy; each nursed anger and resentment.

sentences.zh: 漢人自佷山通武陵，使侍中襄陽馬良以金錦賜五谿諸蠻夷，授以官爵。

translations.literal: Han men from Henshan connected to Wuling; sent Palace Attendant Xiangyang Ma Liang with gold and brocade to bestow on the various Man and Yi of Wuxi, conferring offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: The Han forces opened a route from Mount Hen through to Wuling and sent Palace Attendant Ma Liang of Xiangyang to bestow gold and brocades on the various tribal peoples of Wuxi, conferring offices and titles upon them.

sentences.zh: 6三月，乙丑，立皇子齊公叡為平原王、皇弟鄢陵公彰等皆進爵為王。

translations.literal: 6. Third month, on the day Yichou, established the Emperor's son Prince of Qi Rui as Prince of Pingyuan; the Emperor's younger brothers Prince of Yanling Zhang and others all advanced in rank to princes.
translations.idiomatic: 6. In the third month, on the day Yichou, the Emperor invested his son Cao Rui, Duke of Qi, as Prince of Pingyuan, and his younger brothers, including Cao Zhang, Duke of Yanling, were all advanced to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，立皇子霖為河東王。

translations.literal: On the day Jiaxu, established the Emperor's son Lin as Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiaxu, the Emperor invested his son Cao Lin as Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 7甲午，帝行如襄邑。

translations.literal: 7. On the day Jiawu, the Emperor proceeded to Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: 7. On the day Jiawu, the Emperor proceeded to Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 8夏，四月，戊申，立鄄城侯植為鄄城王。

translations.literal: 8. Summer, fourth month, on the day Wushen, established Marquis of Juancheng Zhi as Prince of Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: 8. In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Wushen, the Emperor invested Marquis of Juancheng Cao Zhi as Prince of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸侯王皆寄地空名而無其實；

translations.literal: At this time, feudatory princes all had registered lands but empty titles without reality;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the feudatory princes held only nominal titles over registered fiefs, without real authority;

sentences.zh: 王國各有老兵百餘人以為守衛；

translations.literal: each princedom had veteran soldiers of a hundred-odd men as guards;
translations.idiomatic: each princedom had only a hundred-odd veteran soldiers for its guard;

sentences.zh: 隔絕千里之外，不聽朝聘，為設防輔監國之官以伺察之。

translations.literal: separated by a thousand li beyond, not permitted court audiences or tribute visits; for them were set defense aides and princely supervisors to observe and investigate them.
translations.idiomatic: they were kept a thousand li away and denied audience at court; officials were appointed as aides and supervisors to watch and report on them.

sentences.zh: 雖有王侯之號而儕於匹夫，皆思為布衣而不能得。

translations.literal: though having titles of princes and marquises yet equaled common men—all wished to become plain-clothed commoners yet could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: though they bore princely titles they were no better than commoners; all longed to live as ordinary men and could not.

sentences.zh: 法既峻切，諸侯王過惡日聞；

translations.literal: laws being already severe and sharp, the princes' transgressions and evils daily heard of;
translations.idiomatic: The laws were harsh, and reports of the princes' misdeeds reached the throne daily;

sentences.zh: 獨北海王兗謹慎好學，未嘗有失。

translations.literal: only the Prince of Beihai, Tan, careful and fond of learning—never had fault.
translations.idiomatic: only the Prince of Beihai, Cao Tan, was conscientious and studious and never gave cause for complaint.

sentences.zh: 文學、防輔相與言曰：「受詔察王舉措，有過當奏，及有善亦宜以聞。

translations.literal: Literary attendants and defense aides together spoke: "Receiving orders to observe the Prince's conduct—if there are faults one ought to memorialize, and if there are virtues also ought to report them.
translations.idiomatic: The literary attendants and defense aides said among themselves: "We are ordered to observe the Prince's conduct; faults must be reported, but virtues should also be reported."

sentences.zh: 」遂共表稱陳兗美。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together submitted a memorial praising Tan's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly submitted a memorial praising Cao Tan's merit.

sentences.zh: 兗聞之，大驚懼，責讓文學曰：「修身自守，常人之行耳，而諸君乃以上聞，是適所以增其負累也。

translations.literal: Tan hearing this, greatly alarmed and fearful, reproached the literary attendants: "Cultivating the person and guarding oneself—ordinary men's conduct only—yet you lords report it above; this precisely adds to one's burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Tan, hearing of this, was greatly alarmed and rebuked the literary attendants: "Self-cultivation is ordinary conduct; yet you report it to the throne—you only increase my burden thereby.

sentences.zh: 且如有善，何患不聞，而遽共如是，是非所以為益也。

translations.literal: Moreover if there are virtues, what worry of not being heard—yet hastily together like this, this is not the way to be of benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If I truly had merit, why worry that it would not be heard? Yet you hasten together in this way—this does no good at all."

sentences.zh: 9癸亥，帝還許昌。

translations.literal: 9. On the day Guihai, the Emperor returned to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 9. On the day Guihai, the Emperor returned to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 10五月，以江南八郡為荊州，江北諸郡為郢州。

translations.literal: 10. Fifth month, made the eight commanderies south of the river into Jing Province, the various commanderies north of the river into Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In the fifth month, the eight commanderies south of the Yangtze were made into Jing Province, and the commanderies north of the river were made into Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 11漢人自巫峽建平連營至夷陵界，立數十屯，以馮習為大督，張南為前部督，自正月與吳相拒，至六月不決。

translations.literal: 11. Han men from Wuxia and Jianping linked camps to the border of Yiling, established several tens of encampments; made Feng Xi Grand Commander, Zhang Nan Front Commander; from the first month confronting Wu to the sixth month undecided.
translations.idiomatic: 11. The Han forces linked camps from the Wuxia Gorge and Jianping eastward to the border of Yiling, establishing dozens of encampments. Feng Xi was made grand commander and Zhang Nan front commander. From the first month they faced Wu without resolution through the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 漢主遣吳班將數千人於平地立營，吳將帥皆欲擊之，陸遜曰：「此必有譎，且觀之。

translations.literal: The Han Lord sent Wu Ban leading several thousand men to establish a camp on level ground; Wu generals all wished to attack; Lu Xun said: "This must have trickery—for the present observe it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler sent Wu Ban with several thousand men to establish a camp on level ground. The Wu commanders all wished to attack, but Lu Xun said: "There must be a stratagem here—let us watch for now."

sentences.zh: 」漢主知其計不行，乃引伏兵八千從谷中出。

translations.literal: " The Han Lord knew his plan would not succeed, thereupon led eight thousand hidden troops out from the valley.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler, seeing his stratagem had failed, withdrew eight thousand ambush troops from the valley.

sentences.zh: 遜曰：「所以不聽諸君擊班者，揣之必有巧故也。

translations.literal: Xun said: "The reason I did not heed you gentlemen in attacking Ban—supposing it, there must be crafty cause.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said: "The reason I would not hear of attacking Wu Ban was that I suspected some crafty design."

sentences.zh: 」遜上疏於吳王曰：「夷陵要害，國之關限，雖為易得，亦復易失。

translations.literal: " Xun submitted a memorial to the King of Wu: "Yiling is a strategic pass, the state's gate and barrier—though easy to obtain, also easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun submitted a memorial to the King of Wu: "Yiling is a strategic chokepoint, the gate and barrier of the state—though it may be taken easily, it may also be lost easily.

sentences.zh: 失之，非徒損一郡之地，荊州可憂，今日爭之，當令必諧。

translations.literal: Lose it—not merely damage one commandery's territory; Jing Province is cause for concern; today's contest over it—ought to make sure it succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: To lose it would not merely forfeit one commandery—it would put all Jing Province at risk. Today's contest must end in success.

sentences.zh: 備干天常，不守窟穴而敢自送，臣雖不材，憑奉威靈，以順討逆，破壞在近，無可憂者。

translations.literal: Bei violates Heaven's constant, does not guard his den yet dares to deliver himself; your subject though lacking talent, relying on and upholding your awesome spirit, with the compliant to punish the rebellious—destruction is near, nothing to worry of.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei has violated Heaven's constant and left his lair to offer himself up. Your subject, though lacking talent, relying on your majesty's authority to punish the rebel with righteousness, sees his destruction close at hand—there is nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 臣初嫌之水陸俱進，今反捨船就步，處處結營，察其佈置，必無他變。

translations.literal: Your subject at first feared his advancing by both land and water; now conversely abandoning boats for foot—everywhere establishing camps; observing his deployment, certainly no other changes.
translations.idiomatic: I had feared he would advance by land and water together, but now he has abandoned his boats for marching on foot and camps everywhere. Observing his disposition, he clearly has no other plan.

sentences.zh: 伏願至尊高枕，不以為念也。

translations.literal: Bowing wish the Supreme One pillow high, not take it to mind.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty may rest easy and give it no further thought."

sentences.zh: 閏月，遜將進攻漢軍，諸將並曰：「攻備當在初，今乃令入五六百里，相守經七八月，其諸要害皆已固守，擊之必無利矣。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Xun was about to advance and attack the Han army; the generals all said: "Attacking Bei should be at the beginning—now he has been allowed in five or six hundred li, holding positions through seven or eight months; all strategic passes are already firmly held—striking will certainly bring no profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, as Lu Xun was about to advance against the Han army, the generals all said: "We ought to have attacked Liu Bei at the outset; now he has been allowed in five or six hundred li and has held his ground for seven or eight months. Every strategic point is firmly defended—an attack can bring no gain."

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「備是猾虜，更嘗事多，其軍始集，思慮精專，未可干也。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "Bei is a cunning captive; experienced in many affairs—when his army first assembled, thoughts and considerations keen and focused, not to be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said: "Liu Bei is a cunning adversary, seasoned in many campaigns; when his army first assembled, his plans were keen and focused, and could not be challenged.

sentences.zh: 今住已久，不得我便，兵疲意沮，計不復生。

translations.literal: Now stationed long already, not obtaining our convenience—troops weary, intent discouraged, plans no longer arising.
translations.idiomatic: Now he has been halted long, we hold the advantage, his troops are weary and dispirited, and his stratagems are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 掎角此寇，正在今日。

translations.literal: Flanking this invader—precisely today.
translations.idiomatic: To take this enemy in a pincer—that time is now."

sentences.zh: 」乃先攻一營，不利，諸將皆曰：「空殺兵耳！

translations.literal: " Thereupon first attacked one camp—not advantageous; the generals all said: "Emptyly killing soldiers only!
translations.idiomatic: He first assaulted one camp without success; the generals all said: "We are wasting our men for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「吾已曉破之之術。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "I already understand the art of breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said: "I already know how to break them."

sentences.zh: 」乃敕各持一把茅，以火攻，拔之；

translations.literal: " Thereupon ordered each to hold a bundle of thatch, with fire attack, took it;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered each man to carry a bundle of thatch, attacked with fire, and overran the camp;

sentences.zh: 一爾勢成，通率諸軍，同時俱攻，斬張南、馮習及胡王沙摩柯等首，破其四十餘營。

translations.literal: in one stroke momentum formed, led through all armies, together at the same time attacked, beheaded Zhang Nan, Feng Xi, and the Barbarian King Shamoke and others; broke their forty-odd camps.
translations.idiomatic: once momentum was gained, he led all the armies in a simultaneous assault, beheading Zhang Nan, Feng Xi, the tribal king Shamoke, and others, and breaking more than forty camps.

sentences.zh: 漢將杜路、劉寧等窮逼請降。

translations.literal: Han generals Du Lu, Liu Ning and others in extremity begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Han generals Du Lu, Liu Ning, and others, driven to the last extremity, begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 漢主升馬鞍山，陳兵自繞，遜督促諸軍，四面蹙之，土崩瓦解，死者萬數。

translations.literal: The Han Lord ascended Mount Ma'an, arrayed troops encircling himself; Xun urged on all armies, from four sides compressed them—earth crumbling, tiles disintegrating; dead numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler ascended Mount Ma'an and drew up his troops in a ring about himself; Lu Xun pressed all his armies forward and closed in from every side—the Han lines collapsed and disintegrated, and the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 漢主夜遁，驛人自擔燒鐃鎧斷後，僅得入白帝城，其舟船、器械，水、步軍資，一時略盡，尸骸塞江而下。

translations.literal: The Han Lord fled by night; courier men themselves carrying and burning gongs, armor to break the rear—barely reaching Baidi City; his boats, weapons, water and foot army supplies—all at once nearly exhausted; corpses blocked the river flowing down.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler fled by night; couriers themselves carried gongs and burned armor to cover the retreat, and he barely reached Baidi City. His boats, weapons, and supplies for the navy and infantry were lost at once; corpses choked the river downstream.

sentences.zh: 漢主大慚恚曰：「吾乃為陸遜所折辱，豈非天耶！

translations.literal: The Han Lord greatly ashamed and resentful said: "I have been shamed and humiliated by Lu Xun—is this not Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler, deeply shamed and bitter, said: "To be broken and humiliated by Lu Xun—is this not Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 」將軍義陽傅肜為後殿，兵眾盡死，肜氣益烈。

translations.literal: " General Fu Rong of Yiyang served as rear guard; the troops all died; Rong's spirit grew the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: " General Fu Rong of Yiyang served as rear guard; his men were all killed, and Rong's fighting spirit grew only fiercer.

sentences.zh: 吳人諭之使降，肜罵曰：「吳狗，安有漢將軍而降者！

translations.literal: The Wu men urged him to surrender; Rong cursed: "Wu dogs—is there a Han general who would surrender!
translations.idiomatic: The Wu soldiers urged him to surrender. Rong cursed them: "Wu dogs! Would a general of Han ever surrender!

sentences.zh: 」遂死之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he died for it.
translations.idiomatic: " He died fighting.

sentences.zh: 從事祭酒程畿溯江而退，眾曰：「後追將至，宜解舫輕行。

translations.literal: Attendant Sacrifices Director Cheng Ji went upriver in retreat; the crowd said: "Pursuers from the rear will soon arrive—one should cast off boats and travel light.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji, the Attendant Director of Sacrifices, retreated upriver. The men said: "The enemy will soon overtake us from behind—we should cast off the boats and travel light."

sentences.zh: 」畿曰：「吾在軍，未習為敵之走也。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "I have been in the army and am not practiced in fleeing before the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji said: "I have served in the army and am not in the habit of fleeing before the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」亦死之。

translations.literal: " He too died for it.
translations.idiomatic: " He too died fighting.

sentences.zh: 初，吳安東中郎將孫桓別擊漢前鋒於夷道，為漢所圍，求救於陸遜，遜曰：「未可。

translations.literal: Initially, Wu Central Guard General of Andong Sun Huan separately attacked the Han vanguard at Yidao and was besieged by Han; he begged Lu Xun for rescue; Xun said: "Not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sun Huan, Central Guard General of Andong under Wu, had attacked the Han vanguard separately at Yidao and been surrounded by Han forces. He appealed to Lu Xun for relief. Xun said: "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「孫安東，公族，見圍已困，奈何不救！

translations.literal: " The generals said: "Sun of Andong is of the ruling clan—besieged and already in distress—why not save him!
translations.idiomatic: " The generals said: "Sun of Andong is of the ruling house, besieged and already in dire straits—why won't you rescue him!"

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「安東得士眾心，城牢糧足，無可憂也。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "Andong has won the hearts of officers and men; the city is strong and provisions ample—nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Xun said: "Andong has won the loyalty of his troops; his walls are strong and his grain ample. There is no cause for worry."

sentences.zh: 待吾計展，欲不救安東，安東自解。

translations.literal: Wait until my plans unfold—if we do not want to rescue Andong, Andong will free himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until my plan takes effect—even if we do not go to Andong's aid, he will break the siege on his own.

sentences.zh: 」及方略大施，漢果奔潰。

translations.literal: " When the strategy was fully deployed, Han indeed fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: " When the plan was fully executed, the Han army broke and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 桓後見遜曰：「前實怨不見救；

translations.literal: Huan afterward saw Xun and said: "Before, I truly resented not being rescued;
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Huan met Lu Xun and said: "I did resent your failure to rescue me;

sentences.zh: 定至今日，乃知調度自有方耳！

translations.literal: fixed to today, then knew deployment and command have their own method!
translations.idiomatic: but only now do I understand that your command truly has its method!"

sentences.zh: 遜按劍曰：「劉備天下知名，曹操所憚，今在境界，此強對也。

translations.literal: Xun grasped his sword and said: "Liu Bei is famous throughout the realm; Cao Cao feared him; now he is at our border—this is a formidable opponent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun grasped his sword and said: "Liu Bei is renowned throughout the realm, and even Cao Cao feared him. Now he stands on our border—this is a formidable foe."

sentences.zh: 諸君並荷國恩，當相輯睦，共翦此虜，上報所受，而不相順，何也？

translations.literal: You gentlemen all bear the nation's grace; ought to help one another in harmony, together cut down this invader, repaying what you have received—yet not obey one another—why?
translations.idiomatic: All of you owe the state a debt of grace. You ought to work together in harmony to destroy this enemy and repay what you owe—yet you will not heed one another. Why?

sentences.zh: 僕雖書生，受命主上，國家所以屈諸君使相承望者，以僕尺寸可稱，能忍辱負重故也。

translations.literal: Although I am but a scholar, I received the mandate of the ruler; the reason the state humbled you gentlemen to place yourselves under my authority is that in me something can be measured, and I can bear humiliation and heavy burdens.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a scholar, yet my ruler entrusted me with command. The state lowered you to serve under me because I am not wholly unfit for the task and because I can swallow humiliation and bear heavy burdens."

sentences.zh: 各在其事，豈復得辭！

translations.literal: Each at his post—how can one still make excuses!
translations.idiomatic: Each of you has his duty—there is no more room for excuses!"

sentences.zh: 軍令有常，不可犯也！

translations.literal: Military orders have fixed rules—one must not violate them!
translations.idiomatic: Military law is fixed and may not be violated!"

sentences.zh: 」及至破備，計多出遜，諸將乃服。

translations.literal: " When they came to defeating Bei, most plans came from Xun; the generals then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " When Liu Bei was finally defeated, most of the strategy had come from Lu Xun, and the generals at last submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 吳王聞之曰：「公何以初不啟諸將違節度者邪？

translations.literal: The King of Wu hearing it said: "Sir, why at first did you not report those generals who violated command structure?
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Wu heard of this, he asked: "Why did you not report the generals who disobeyed orders at the outset?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「受恩深重，此諸將或任腹心，或堪爪牙，或是功臣，皆國家所當與共克定大事者，臣竊慕相如、寇恂相下之義以濟國事。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Receiving grace deeply and heavily—these generals some serve as trusted intimates, some serve as claws and fangs, some are meritorious ministers—all are ones the state ought to share with in conquering and settling great affairs; your servant privately admires the meaning of Lin Xiangru and Kou Xun yielding to each other to accomplish state business.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "I owe the state a great debt. These generals are trusted intimates, capable instruments, or meritorious servants—all men the state must rely on to settle great affairs. I privately resolved to emulate Lin Xiangru and Kou Xun, who humbled themselves before each other for the good of the state."

sentences.zh: 」王大笑稱善，加遜輔國將軍，領荊州牧，改封江陵侯。

translations.literal: " The King laughed greatly and praised it; added Xun as Assistant State General, administering as Governor of Jing Province, changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: " The King laughed and praised him. Lu Xun was promoted to Assistant State General, made Governor of Jing Province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，諸葛亮與尚書令法正好尚不同，而以公義相取，亮每奇正智術。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhuge Liang and Director of the Masters of Writing Fa Zheng had different personal inclinations, yet by public duty they valued each other; Liang always admired Zheng's wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang and Fa Zheng, Director of the Masters of Writing, differed in personal taste, yet they respected each other in the service of the state, and Liang always admired Fa Zheng's intelligence and skill.

sentences.zh: 及漢主伐吳而敗，時正已卒，亮歎曰：「孝直若在，必能制主上東行。

translations.literal: When the Han Lord attacked Wu and was defeated, Zheng had already died; Liang sighed: "If Xiaozhi were alive, he would surely be able to restrain the Lord's eastern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han ruler's attack on Wu ended in defeat, Fa Zheng was already dead. Zhuge Liang sighed and said: "If Xiaozhi were still alive, he would surely have restrained our lord from marching east."

sentences.zh: 就使東行，必不傾危矣。

translations.literal: Even if he went east, he would surely not topple into peril.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he had marched east, disaster would surely not have befallen us."

sentences.zh: 」漢主在白帝，徐盛、潘璋、宋謙等各競表言「備必可禽，乞復攻之。

translations.literal: " The Han Lord was at Baidi; Xu Sheng, Pan Zhang, Song Qian and others each competed in memorials saying "Bei can surely be captured—we beg to attack again.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han ruler was at Baidi. Xu Sheng, Pan Zhang, Song Qian, and others each sent urgent memorials declaring that Liu Bei could surely be taken and begging permission to attack again."

sentences.zh: 」吳王以問陸遜。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu asked Lu Xun about it.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Wu consulted Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜與朱然、駱統上言曰：「曹丕大合士眾，外托助國討備，內實有奸心，謹決計輒還。

translations.literal: Xun with Zhu Ran and Luo Tong memorialized saying: "Cao Pi has greatly assembled officers and men; outwardly claiming to aid the state in punishing Bei, inwardly in fact harboring treacherous intent—we respectfully decide and immediately return.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, Zhu Ran, and Luo Tong memorialized: "Cao Pi has massed a large army. Outwardly he claims to help us punish Liu Bei, but inwardly he harbors treacherous designs. We respectfully resolve to withdraw at once."

sentences.zh: 初，帝聞漢兵樹柵連營七百餘里，謂群臣曰：「備不曉兵，豈有七百里營可以拒敵者乎！

translations.literal: Initially, the Emperor heard the Han army had planted palisades and linked camps for more than seven hundred li; he told the ministers: "Bei does not understand warfare—is there a camp of seven hundred li that can resist the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first heard that the Han army had planted palisades and linked camps for more than seven hundred li, he told his ministers: "Liu Bei knows nothing of war. Can a line of camps seven hundred li long possibly hold off an enemy?"

sentences.zh: 『苞原隰險阻而為軍者為敵所禽』，此兵忌也。

translations.literal: 'Making camp among marshes, lowlands, and difficult terrain, one is captured by the enemy'—this is a military taboo.
translations.idiomatic: 'A host that encamps amid marshland, low ground, and rough terrain will be taken by the enemy'—that is a fundamental military taboo."

sentences.zh: 孫權上事今至矣。

translations.literal: Sun Quan's report on the campaign ought to arrive now.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's report of victory ought to arrive any day now."

sentences.zh: 」後七日，吳破漢書到。

translations.literal: " Seven days later, Wu's report of breaking Han arrived.
translations.idiomatic: " Seven days later, the dispatch from Wu announcing the defeat of Han arrived.

sentences.zh: 12秋，七月，冀州大蝗，饑。

translations.literal: 12th year, autumn, seventh month—Jizhou had great locusts; famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, in the seventh month of autumn, Jizhou suffered a plague of locusts and famine.

sentences.zh: 13漢主既敗走，黃權在江北，道絕，不得還，八月，率其眾來降。

translations.literal: 13th year—The Han Lord having been defeated and fled, Huang Quan was north of the river; the route cut off, unable to return; eighth month, he led his multitude to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, after the Han ruler's defeat and flight, Huang Quan was stranded north of the river with his escape cut off. In the eighth month he led his troops to surrender.

sentences.zh: 漢有司請收權妻子，漢主曰：「孤負黃權，權不負孤也。

translations.literal: Han officials requested seizing Quan's wife and children; the Han Lord said: "I have failed Huang Quan—Quan has not failed me.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials asked to arrest Huang Quan's wife and children. The Han ruler said: "I have wronged Huang Quan; Huang Quan has not wronged me."

sentences.zh: 」待之如初。

translations.literal: " Treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He treated them as before.

sentences.zh: 帝謂權曰：「君捨逆效順，欲追蹤陳、韓邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Quan: "Sir, you abandoned rebellion and obeyed—do you wish to follow in the footsteps of Chen She and Han Xin?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Huang Quan: "You have abandoned the rebel cause and come over to us. Do you wish to emulate Chen She and Han Xin?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣過受劉主殊遇，降吳不可，還蜀無路，是以歸命。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant excessively received Lord Liu's special favor; surrendering to Wu was impossible, returning to Shu had no road—therefore submitted to your mandate.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "I received extraordinary favor from Lord Liu. I could not surrender to Wu, and I had no road back to Shu. That is why I submit to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 且敗軍之將，免死為幸，何古人之可慕也！

translations.literal: Moreover, a general of a defeated army—to escape death is already fortunate—what ancients are there to emulate!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a defeated general is lucky to escape with his life. What ancient hero is there for me to emulate!"

sentences.zh: 」帝善之，拜為鎮南將軍，封育陽侯，加侍中，使陪乘。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised him; appointed him as Pacifying South General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuyang, added as Palace Attendant, and had him ride in the accompanying chariot.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased and appointed Huang Quan Pacifying South General, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuyang, made him Palace Attendant, and had him ride in the imperial escort chariot.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「臣與劉、葛推誠相信，明臣本志。

translations.literal: Quan said: "Your servant with Liu and Ge gave sincere trust and belief, making clear your servant's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan said: "Lord Liu and Zhuge and I trusted each other fully. That should make my true intentions plain."

sentences.zh: 竊疑未實，請須。

translations.literal: I privately suspect it is not true—please wait.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect this is untrue. I beg leave to wait and see."

sentences.zh: 」後得審問，果如所言。

translations.literal: " Later obtained investigation and inquiry—indeed as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: " Later investigation proved it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 馬良亦死於五谿。

translations.literal: Ma Liang also died at Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang also died at Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 14九月，甲午，詔曰：「夫婦人與政，亂之本也。

translations.literal: 14th year, ninth month, day Jiawu—an edict said: "Women participating in government is the root of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, on the day Jiawu in the ninth month, an edict declared: "When women take part in government, disorder follows."

sentences.zh: 自今以後，群臣不得奏事太后，后族之家不得當輔政之任，又不得橫受茅士之爵。

translations.literal: From now onward, ministers may not submit business to the Empress Dowager; families of the empress's clan may not hold the role of assisting in government, nor may they wantonly receive marquisates of fief territory.
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, ministers may not submit affairs to the Empress Dowager. The empress's kin may not hold offices of regency, nor may they freely receive noble fiefs.

sentences.zh: 以此詔傳之後世，若有背違，天下共誅之。

translations.literal: Take this edict and pass it to later generations—if any violate it, all under Heaven shall join in punishing them.
translations.idiomatic: Let this edict be handed down to later generations. Whoever violates it, the whole realm shall join in punishing him."

sentences.zh: 」卞太后每見外親，不假以顏色，常言：「居處當節儉，不當望賞，念自佚也。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Bian whenever she saw outer kin, did not lend them an agreeable countenance; she often said: "In dwelling one ought to be frugal—one ought not expect reward, thinking to indulge oneself.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Bian never showed kindness when she received her kinsmen from outside the palace. She often said: "Live frugally. Do not expect gifts or rewards, thinking only to indulge yourselves."

sentences.zh: 外捨當怪吾遇之太薄，吾自有常度故也。

translations.literal: Outsiders ought to think my treatment of them too thin—I have my own fixed measure for this.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders may think me too cold, but I have my own standards."

sentences.zh: 吾事武帝四五十年，行儉日久，不能自變為奢。

translations.literal: I served Emperor Wu for forty or fifty years; practicing frugality long—I cannot by myself change to extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: I served Emperor Wu for forty or fifty years and grew accustomed to thrift. I cannot suddenly turn to extravagance.

sentences.zh: 有犯科禁者，吾且能加罪一等耳，莫望錢米恩貸也。

translations.literal: If any violate statutes and prohibitions, I can only increase guilt by one degree—do not hope for money, grain, or grace in loans.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you break the law, I will only increase your punishment by one degree. Do not expect money, grain, or any special favor from me."

sentences.zh: 15帝將立郭貴嬪為后，中郎棧潛上疏曰：「夫后妃之德，盛衰治亂所由生也。

translations.literal: 15th year—The Emperor was about to install Lady Guo the Honored Consort as empress; Palace Gentleman Zhan Qian submitted a memorial saying: "The virtue of empress and consort is that from which rise and fall, order and disorder are born.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when the Emperor was about to install Honored Consort Guo as empress, Palace Gentleman Zhan Qian submitted a memorial: "The character of empress and consort is the source from which a state's rise and fall, order and chaos, proceed."

sentences.zh: 是以聖哲慎立元妃，必取先代世族之家，擇其令淑，以統六宮，虔奉宗廟。

translations.literal: Therefore sage and wise rulers are careful in establishing the primary consort; they must take from families of former generations' noble houses, choose those who are fine and virtuous, to preside over the six palaces and devoutly attend the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: That is why sage rulers take great care in choosing a principal consort, selecting women of ancient noble lineage who are virtuous and gentle to preside over the inner palace and serve the ancestral shrines with devotion.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『家道正而天下定。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'When the way of the household is upright, all under Heaven is settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 'When the way of the household is correct, the realm is settled.'

sentences.zh: 』由內及外，先王之令典也。

translations.literal: ' From within reaching outward—this is the former kings' authoritative precedent.
translations.idiomatic: ' To govern from within outward is the authoritative precedent of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書宗人釁夏云：『無以妾為夫人之禮。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn Annals records Zongren Xingxia saying: 'Do not use the rites for making a concubine into the Lady.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records Officer of the Ancestral Temple Xing Xia as saying: 'There is no rite by which a concubine may be made the principal wife.'

sentences.zh: 』齊桓誓命於葵丘，亦曰：『無以妾為妻。

translations.literal: ' Duke Huan of Qi swore his mandate at Kuqiu, also saying: 'Do not take a concubine as wife.
translations.idiomatic: ' Duke Huan of Qi likewise swore at Kuiqiu: 'Do not make a concubine your wife.'

sentences.zh: 』令後宮嬖寵，常亞乘輿，若因愛登后，使賤人暴貴，臣恐後世下陵上替，開張非度，亂自上起。

translations.literal: ' Today the favored of the inner palace constantly rank below the imperial carriage; if through love one installs one as empress, making a low person suddenly exalted—your servant fears later generations will see inferiors subvert superiors, open wide unorthodox measures, and disorder arise from above.
translations.idiomatic: ' Today the emperor's favorites in the inner palace always rank below the imperial chariot. If affection elevates a low-born woman to empress and grants a humble person sudden glory, I fear later ages will see subjects overturn rulers, propriety give way to license, and disorder rise from the very top."

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 庚子，立皇后郭氏。

translations.literal: Day Gengzi—installed Empress Guo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengzi, Empress Guo was installed.

sentences.zh: 16初，吳王遣于禁護軍浩周、軍司馬東里袞詣帝，自陳誠款，辭甚恭愨。

translations.literal: 16th year, initially—The King of Wu sent Yu Jin's Protector of the Army Hao Zhou and Army Major Dongli Gun to the Emperor, personally stating sincerity and good faith; the words very respectful and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the King of Wu sent Protector of the Army Hao Zhou and Army Major Dongli Gun to the Emperor, declaring his sincere submission in language of deep respect and earnest devotion.

sentences.zh: 帝問周等：「權可信乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Zhou and others: "Can Quan be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Zhou and the others: "Can Sun Quan be trusted?"

sentences.zh: 」周以為權必臣服，而袞謂其不可必服。

translations.literal: " Zhou thought Quan would surely submit; but Gun said he could not be counted on to submit.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao Zhou thought Sun Quan would surely submit, but Dongli Gun said he could not be relied upon to do so.

sentences.zh: 帝悅周言，以為有以知之，故立為吳王，復使周至吳。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased with Zhou's words, thinking he had grounds for knowing; therefore installed him as King of Wu, and again sent Zhou to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored Zhou's view, believing he had grounds for his judgment, and therefore enfeoffed Sun Quan as King of Wu. He again sent Zhou to Wu.

sentences.zh: 周謂吳王曰：「陛下未信王遣子入侍，周以闔門百口明之。

translations.literal: Zhou said to the King of Wu: "Your Majesty does not yet believe the King sends his son to serve at court—Zhou vouches with my whole household of a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhou told the King of Wu: "If Your Majesty doubts whether the King of Wu will send his son to serve at court, I stake my entire household of a hundred lives upon it."

sentences.zh: 」吳王為之流涕沾襟，指天為誓。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu for this wept until tears soaked his robe collar, pointed to Heaven and swore.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan wept until his tears soaked his robes and swore an oath to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 周還而侍子不至，但多設虛辭。

translations.literal: Zhou returned yet the hostage son did not arrive—only many empty words were set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhou returned, but no hostage son arrived—only empty promises.

sentences.zh: 帝欲遣侍中辛毗、尚書桓階往與盟誓，並責任子，吳王辭讓不受。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to send Palace Attendant Xin Pi and Director of the Masters of Writing Huan Jie to covenant by oath, and also press for the hostage son; the King of Wu declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to send Palace Attendant Xin Pi and Director of the Masters of Writing Huan Jie to negotiate an oath of alliance and to press for the hostage son. The King of Wu declined.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲伐之，劉曄曰：「彼新得志，上下齊心，而阻帶江湖，不可倉卒制也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and wished to attack him; Liu Ye said: "They have newly achieved their aim; above and below of one mind—yet blocked and girded by rivers and lakes—one cannot quickly subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angry and prepared to attack. Liu Ye said: "They have just won a great victory and stand united from top to bottom. Their land is defended by rivers and lakes. They cannot be subdued in haste."

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 九月，命征東大將軍曹休、前將軍張遼、鎮東將軍臧霸出洞口，大將軍曹仁出濡須，上軍大將軍曹真、征南大將軍夏侯尚、左將軍張郃、右將軍徐晃圍南郡。

translations.literal: Ninth month—ordered Campaign-East Grand General Cao Xiu, Forward General Zhang Liao, Pacifying-East General Zang Ba to exit Dongkou; Grand General Cao Ren to exit Ruxu; Upper Army Grand General Cao Zhen, Campaign-South Grand General Xiahou Shang, Left General Zhang He, Right General Xu Huang to besiege Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he ordered Campaign-East Grand General Cao Xiu, Forward General Zhang Liao, and Pacifying-East General Zang Ba to advance from Dongkou; Grand General Cao Ren to advance from Ruxu; Upper Army Grand General Cao Zhen, Campaign-South Grand General Xiahou Shang, Left General Zhang He, and Right General Xu Huang to besiege Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 吳建威將軍呂範督五軍，以舟軍拒休等，左將軍諸葛瑾、平北將軍潘璋、將軍楊粲救南郡，裨將軍朱桓以濡須督拒曹仁。

translations.literal: Wu Establishing Prestige General Lu Fan directed five armies, with the navy to resist Xiu and others; Left General Zhuge Jin, Pacifying-North General Pan Zhang, General Yang Can to rescue Nan Commandery; Vice General Zhu Huan as Supervisor of Ruxu to resist Cao Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's Establishing Prestige General Lu Fan commanded five armies and met Cao Xiu's forces with the navy. Left General Zhuge Jin, Pacifying North General Pan Zhang, and General Yang Can marched to relieve Nan Commandery. Vice General Zhu Huan, as Supervisor of Ruxu, held Cao Ren at bay.

sentences.zh: 17冬，十月，甲子，表首陽山東為壽陵，作終制，務從儉薄，不藏金玉，一用瓦器。

translations.literal: 17th year, winter, tenth month, day Jiazi—nominated the east of Mount Shouyang as Shou Mausoleum; made final regulations, striving for frugality and plainness—no storing gold or jade, using only earthenware vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, on the day Jiazi in the tenth month of winter, he designated the eastern slope of Mount Shouyang as the site of the Shou Mausoleum and wrote his final instructions, insisting on thrift: no gold or jade for burial, only earthenware vessels.

sentences.zh: 令以此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、秘書、三府。

translations.literal: Ordered this edict be stored in the ancestral temple; copies in the Masters of Writing, Palace Secretariat, and Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the edict stored in the ancestral temple, with copies kept by the Masters of Writing, the Palace Secretariat, and the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 18吳王以揚越蠻夷多未平集，乃卑辭上書，求自改厲；

translations.literal: 18th year—The King of Wu, because the Yang-Yue barbarians were largely not yet pacified and gathered, then with humble words submitted a letter, asking to reform and discipline himself;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, because many of the Yang-Yue tribal peoples had not yet been pacified, the King of Wu wrote humbly to the Emperor, pledging to reform himself;

sentences.zh: 「若罪在難除，必不見置，當奉還土地民人，寄命交州以終餘年。

translations.literal: "If my crimes are hard to remove and I will surely not be spared, I shall return the land and people, entrusting my life to Jiao Province to end my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: "If my crimes are beyond forgiveness and I cannot be pardoned, I will return my lands and people and spend my last years in Jiao Province."

sentences.zh: 」又與浩周書云：「欲為子登求昏宗室。

translations.literal: " Again wrote to Hao Zhou saying: "Wish to seek marriage in the imperial clan for my son Deng.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote to Hao Zhou: "I wish to seek an imperial bride for my son Deng."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「以登年弱，欲遣孫長緒、張子布隨登俱來。

translations.literal: " Also said: "Because Deng is young in years, wish to send Sun Changxu and Zhang Zibu to accompany Deng and come together.
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "Because Deng is still young, I wish to send Sun Changxu and Zhang Zibu to accompany him."

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「朕之與君，大義已定，豈樂勞師遠臨江、漢！

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied: "Between Us and you, the great principle is already settled—how would We delight in laboring armies to come from afar to the Yangtze and Han!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied: "The bond between us is already settled in principle. Would I take pleasure in marching armies far to the Yangtze and the Han!"

sentences.zh: 若登身朝到，夕召兵還耳。

translations.literal: If Deng himself arrives at court in the morning, by evening We summon the armies back.
translations.idiomatic: If Deng presents himself at court in the morning, I will recall my armies by evening."

sentences.zh: 」於是吳王改元黃武，臨江拒守。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the King of Wu changed the era name to Huangwu, faced the river and resisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the King of Wu changed his era name to Huangwu and took up positions along the Yangtze to resist invasion.

sentences.zh: 帝自許昌南征，復郢州為荊州。

translations.literal: The Emperor from Xuchang marched south on campaign; restored Ying Province to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marched south from Xuchang on campaign and restored the name Jing Province to what had been called Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛丑，帝如宛。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day Xinchou—the Emperor proceeded to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day Xinchou, the Emperor went to Wan.

sentences.zh: 曹休在洞口，自陳：「願將銳卒虎步江南，因敵取資，事必克捷，若其無臣，不須為念。

translations.literal: Cao Xiu was at Dongkou and personally stated: "I wish to lead sharp soldiers, treading the Jiangnan like tigers, taking provisions from the enemy—affairs will surely be swiftly victorious; if there is no servant, need not think of me.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu, at Dongkou, memorialized: "I beg leave to lead elite troops in a tiger's stride across the Jiangnan, living off the enemy. Victory is certain. If I fail, Your Majesty need not grieve for me."

sentences.zh: 」帝恐休便渡江，驛馬止之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor feared Xiu would promptly cross the river; courier horses stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor feared Cao Xiu would cross the Yangtze too hastily and sent relay horses to halt him.

sentences.zh: 侍中董昭侍側，曰：「竊見陛下有憂色，獨以休濟江故乎？

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Dong Zhao waited at his side and said: "I privately see Your Majesty has a worried expression—is it solely because of Xiu crossing the river?
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Dong Zhao, standing at his side, said: "I notice Your Majesty looks troubled—is it only because Cao Xiu is crossing the Yangtze?

sentences.zh: 今者渡江，人情所難，就休有此志，勢不獨行，當須諸將。

translations.literal: At present crossing the river is what human sentiment finds difficult; even if Xiu has such a will, the situation will not allow him to act alone—he must rely on the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river is hard for any army. Even if Cao Xiu is eager to go, he cannot move alone—he will need the other generals.

sentences.zh: 臧霸等既富且貴，無復他望，但欲終其天年，保守祿祚而已，何肯乘危自投死地以求徼倖！

translations.literal: Zang Ba and the others are already wealthy and ennobled, with no other ambition—they only wish to live out their natural span and preserve their stipends and rank—how would they be willing to take advantage of danger and throw themselves into a dead place seeking luck!
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba and the others are already rich and honored, with nothing left to seek but to live out their days and keep their stipends and rank. Why would they risk everything by plunging into mortal danger for a desperate gamble!

sentences.zh: 苟霸等不進，休意自沮。

translations.literal: If Ba and the others do not advance, Xiu's intent will naturally be discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: If Zang Ba and the others refuse to advance, Cao Xiu's resolve will collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 臣恐陛下雖有敕渡之詔，猶必沉吟，未便從命也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that even if Your Majesty has an edict ordering the crossing, you will still hesitate and not readily obey.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that even if Your Majesty issues an order to cross, Cao Xiu will still hesitate and not obey at once.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，會暴風吹吳呂範等船，綆纜悉斷，直詣休等營下，斬首獲生以千數，吳兵迸散。

translations.literal: " Before long, a violent wind blew the ships of Wu's Lü Fan and others—the mooring ropes all snapped—they went straight to Xiu's and the others' camps, beheaded and captured prisoners by the thousands, and Wu troops scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward, a violent storm struck the Wu ships under Lü Fan and others, snapping every mooring line and driving them straight into Cao Xiu's camp. Thousands were killed or captured, and the Wu army broke apart.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，敕諸軍促渡。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it and ordered all armies to hasten the crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this, he ordered all his armies to cross the river at once.

sentences.zh: 軍未時進，吳救船遂至，收軍還江南。

translations.literal: Before the armies could advance in time, Wu rescue ships arrived; they gathered their troops and returned south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Wei armies could advance, Wu relief ships arrived; the Wu forces regrouped and withdrew south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 曹休使臧霸追之，不利，將軍尹盧戰死。

translations.literal: Cao Xiu sent Zang Ba in pursuit; it went poorly, and General Yin Lu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu sent Zang Ba in pursuit, but the effort failed; General Yin Lu was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 19庚申晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 19. On the last day of Gengshen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 19. On the last day of Gengshen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 20吳王使太中大夫鄭泉聘於漢<ref>吳王使太中大夫鄭泉聘於漢句按據方北辰《三國志蜀書札記》考証，主動求和並先遣使者者是劉備，而非孫權在先。

translations.literal: 20. The King of Wu sent Grand Palace Attendant Zheng Quan on a mission to Han<ref>On the sentence 'The King of Wu sent Grand Palace Attendant Zheng Quan on a mission to Han,' according to Fang Beichen's Notes on the Shu Records of the Three Kingdoms, the one who actively sought peace and first dispatched envoys was Liu Bei, not Sun Quan first.
translations.idiomatic: 20. The King of Wu sent Grand Palace Attendant Zheng Quan on a mission to Han<ref>[Editorial note: According to Fang Beichen's Notes on the Shu Records of the Three Kingdoms, Liu Bei—not Sun Quan—was the one who actively sought peace and first sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 《蜀志．先主傳》章武二年（

translations.literal: Records of Shu, Annals of the Former Lord, Zhangwu year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Shu, Annals of the Former Lord, Zhangwu year 2 (

sentences.zh: 云：「冬十月，孫權聞先主住白帝，甚懼，遣使求和。

translations.literal: It states: "In the tenth month of winter, Sun Quan heard that the Former Lord was stationed at Baidi and was greatly afraid; he sent envoys to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: states: "In the tenth month of winter, Sun Quan heard that Liu Bei was at Baidi and was greatly alarmed; he sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 先主許之，遣太中大夫宗瑋報命。

translations.literal: The Former Lord consented and sent Grand Palace Attendant Zong Wei in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei agreed and sent Grand Palace Attendant Zong Wei in reply.

sentences.zh: 」《吳志．孫權傳》黃武元年（

translations.literal: " Records of Wu, Biography of Sun Quan, Huangwu year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: " The Records of Wu, Biography of Sun Quan, Huangwu year 1 (

sentences.zh: 云：「十二月，權使太中大夫鄭泉聘劉備于白帝，始復通也。

translations.literal: It states: "In the twelfth month, Quan sent Grand Palace Attendant Zheng Quan to visit Liu Bei at Baidi, and relations were restored.
translations.idiomatic: states: "In the twelfth month, Sun Quan sent Grand Palace Attendant Zheng Quan to visit Liu Bei at Baidi, and diplomatic contact was restored.

sentences.zh: 」以上所引的《先主傳》、《吳主傳》兩段史文相比較，就會發現問題：劉備派遣宗瑋，時在冬十月；

translations.literal: " Comparing the two passages quoted above from the Annals of the Former Lord and the Biography of the Ruler of Wu, a problem emerges: Liu Bei dispatched Zong Wei in the tenth month of winter;
translations.idiomatic: " Comparing these two passages from the Annals of the Former Lord and the Biography of the Ruler of Wu, the problem becomes clear: Liu Bei dispatched Zong Wei in the tenth month of winter;

sentences.zh: 孫權派遣鄭泉，時為冬十二月。

translations.literal: Sun Quan dispatched Zheng Quan in the twelfth month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan dispatched Zheng Quan in the twelfth month of winter.

sentences.zh: 也就是，宗瑋東下在先，鄭泉西上在後，其間有兩月之差。

translations.literal: That is, Zong Wei went east first and Zheng Quan went west afterward, with a two-month gap between them.
translations.idiomatic: In other words, Zong Wei went east first and Zheng Quan went west afterward—a gap of two months between them.

sentences.zh: 既然宗瑋東下在先，自然求和的主動者便應當是劉備，而非孫權。

translations.literal: Since Zong Wei went east first, the one who actively sought peace should naturally have been Liu Bei, not Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zong Wei went east first, Liu Bei—not Sun Quan—must have been the one who took the initiative in seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 司馬光綜合《先主傳》及《吳主傳》史文，卻未察覺宗瑋先于鄭泉兩月前往孫吳，致使次第出現顛倒。

translations.literal: Sima Guang synthesized the texts of the Annals of the Former Lord and the Biography of the Ruler of Wu but failed to notice that Zong Wei went to Sun Wu two months before Zheng Quan, causing the sequence to be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang combined the texts of the Annals of the Former Lord and the Biography of the Ruler of Wu but failed to notice that Zong Wei reached Sun Wu two months before Zheng Quan, reversing the order of events.

sentences.zh: </ref>，漢太中大夫宗瑋報之，吳、漢復通。

translations.literal: </ref>, Han Grand Palace Attendant Zong Wei replied; Wu and Han restored relations.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] Han Grand Palace Attendant Zong Wei replied in turn, and Wu and Han restored diplomatic contact.

sentences.zh: 21漢主聞魏師大出，遺陸遜書曰：「賊今已在江、漢，吾將復東，將軍謂其能然否？

translations.literal: 21. The Han Ruler heard that Wei forces were coming out in strength; he sent Lu Xun a letter saying: "The rebels are now already at the Jiang and Han—I will move east again. General, do you think they can do so?
translations.idiomatic: 21. When the Han Ruler heard that Wei was mobilizing in force, he wrote to Lu Xun: "The enemy is now on the Yangtze and Han rivers. I plan to march east again. Do you think they can do so?

sentences.zh: 」遜答曰：「但恐軍新破，創夷未復，始求通親；

translations.literal: " Lu Xun replied: "I only fear the army has been newly defeated, wounds and losses have not yet recovered, and they have just begun to seek kinship ties;
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Xun replied: "I only fear their army has just been defeated, their wounds are not yet healed, and they have only just begun to seek peace through kinship ties;

sentences.zh: 且當自補，未暇窮兵耳。

translations.literal: and they must repair themselves—they have no leisure for exhausting warfare.
translations.idiomatic: They must rebuild their strength and will have no time to exhaust themselves in war.

sentences.zh: 若不推算，欲復以傾覆之餘遠送以來者，無所逃命。

translations.literal: If they do not reckon carefully and wish again to send troops from their overturned remnants from afar, they will have no escape from death.
translations.idiomatic: If they fail to reckon carefully and try again to send their shattered remnants from afar, they will have nowhere to flee.

sentences.zh: 22漢漢嘉太守黃元叛。

translations.literal: 22. Han Hanjia Administrator Huang Yuan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: 22. Huang Yuan, the Hanjia administrator of Han, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 23吳將孫盛督萬人據江陵中洲，以為南郡外援。

translations.literal: 23. Wu general Sun Sheng commanded ten thousand men holding the central islet at Jiangling as external support for Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 23. Wu general Sun Sheng commanded ten thousand men holding the central islet at Jiangling to serve as external support for Nan Commandery.
